The Wellness You Desire is fully committed to the health and wellness of all women, mothers, and families but the focus is on Black, Brown, and Indigenous peoples.

column5: Content Creator Intern - LaGuardia Community College
column6: WHO WE ARE:  The Office of Communications and External Affairs works with a group of student collaborators who contribute to multimedia projects for the college's official Social Media channels and website. column5: 2026 Summer Career Launch Corps - Queens Botanical Garden Education Intern
column6: PLEASE INSERT ALL THE REQUESTED INFORMATION BELOW:    WHO WE ARE:  Queens Botanical Garden (QBG) is a private non-profit cultural institution located on 39 acres of New York City public land in Flushing, New York. A recently completed visitor survey reveals that 45% of visitors speak a language other than English at home. This fact underscores the importance of the mission and the challenges and opportunities QBG faces daily in creating programs, exhibits and landscapes that serve the needs of people who live in and visit one of the most ethnically diverse counties in the nation. The Garden has committed itself to addressing the complex and ever-changing needs of its diverse community and to being the place where people, plants, and cultures meet. Intern will be part of a larger NYC SCI-Network program and will have access/be invited to networking and professional opportunities across our cultural partners.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  The Education Intern will work with Youth Programs Instructors to support the needs of children's programming. Under the supervision of QBG Education staff, interns will work with children to facilitate lessons during our seasonal programs. Tasks include assisting instructors to teach and prepare materials, maintenance of garden plots, supporting Children's learning through various gardening and art activities, and cleaning up after programs. Must be committed to being present and punctual on workdays.     During the summer internship, the intern will specifically support our extended hours program (similar to after-school) for Summer Children’s Garden. On days with low or no attendance, the intern will support with administrative tasks (such as creating newsletters) and gardening.    QBG’s Youth Programs bring together youngsters ages 2 to 14 from around New York City to enjoy seasonal, hands-on learning and gardening experiences year-round. Our young gardeners explore concepts of ecological balance, sustainability, and conservation as they learn how to prepare soil, select seeds and plants, and care for and later harvest their own vegetables, flowers, and herbs that they turn into nutritious and delicious snacks in the classroom. We explore these concepts at age-appropriate levels throughout each season. We strive to create an immersive experience in all programs- a blend of structured and freeform exploration designed to provide children with the support they need to express their natural curiosity.    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  CUNY interns will learn about the inner-workings of a cultural institution's ongoing children's programing. They will gain valuable skills in facilitating programming and maintaining a garden space designed for small hands. The intern will also gain experience in working as part of a professional team with diverse academic and career backgrounds, evaluating the effectiveness of our current models, researching alternative models and collaborating with staff. This position offers very useful experience to individuals interested in entering the non-profit Education sector, museum education, environmental education, informal education and/or early childhood education. Opportunity will include administrative, teaching, and gardening work.    WORK SCHEDULE:  DAYS/TIME: Mondays through Thursdays 1:15-6pm. NOTE: Training to be provided week of June 29 through July 2nd, 8am-4pm each day. Attendance is required.    LOCATION: Location: 43-50 Main Street, Flushing NY 11355  This position is on-site, but we are ADA compliant. Please note the job will require bending, lifting, etc. to garden & work with children. We can provide a virtual option to accommodate occasional sick days, but cannot provide a fully virtual internship.

Who We Are:  This internship is led by Art Beyond Sight through Project Access for All, in active partnership with Disability Pride NYC, Disability Unite, and a broad consortium of disability, cultural, athletic, civic, and public-sector partners citywide. Originally developed through federal and New York City disability workgroups, Project Access for All established a lasting framework for local and national collaboration. The internship is supervised by Art Beyond Sight staff, with regular mentorship meetings from leaders across this consortium, providing hands-on experience and strategic insight into how large-scale accessibility initiatives are built, implemented, and sustained.    Art Beyond Sight leads Project Access for All, the first and only open-source national platform advancing accessibility, inclusion, and systemic change across arts, culture, recreation, and civic life. Through Project Access NYC and the launch of NYC Belongs, we are building district-level partnerships across all 51 City Council districts to strengthen community accessibility infrastructure.    We work at the intersection of disability leadership, cultural institutions, parks and athletics, technology, youth engagement, and public policy — ensuring that access is not an afterthought, but part of how New York City leads. We partner with Disability Pride NYC and Disability Unite—including the annual Disability Unite Festival—and collaborate closely with Independent Living Centers, disability advocacy organizations, arts and cultural institutions, parks and athletic organizations, and entertainment venues across the city.    NYC Belongs is powered by emerging leaders ready to build real change. Through this summer initiative, students gain direct, hands-on engagement with the diverse stakeholders that shape our communities — from grassroots disability advocates to major civic and cultural institutions — building practical skills, professional confidence, and meaningful relationships while advancing systemic change.    NYC Belongs is a fast-moving, multi-team initiative with many moving parts. We are building something ambitious — and we are committed to doing it in a way that is organized, sustainable, and human-centered.

column5: Research Intern - Clinical Directors Network, Inc. (CDN)
column6: WHO WE ARE:  Clinical Directors Network, Inc. (CDN) is a not-for-profit clinician membership organization, practice-based research network (PBRN), and clinician training organization, founded to provide peer-initiated activities for clinicians practicing in low-income, minority, and other underserved communities. CDN’s overall goal is to translate clinical research into clinical practice for the enhancement of health equity and improvement of public health. CDN is the oldest and largest PBRN devoted to providing and improving comprehensive and accessible community-oriented primary and preventive health care services for poor, minority, and underserved populations. CDN operates as a private, not-for-profit corporation, by and for an extensive network of current and future Health Center Clinical Leaders. CDN conducts project-based research and educational activities in partnership with government, academic, not-for-profit, and for-profit organizations.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  • Assist with identifying and recruiting patients for participation in clinical studies.  • Assist with conducting retention activities.  • Identify health educational materials.  • Enter and compile data from assessments.  • Conduct quality assurance checks of intervention and evaluation data.  • Work with “big data” and public data sets.  • Compile evaluation data.  • Conduct literature reviews and assist with the development of new grants.  • Perform clerical and administrative tasks.  • Other duties as assigned.    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  • Ability to develop and evaluate practice-based research projects.  • Data management, including cleaning and managing data from large randomized controlled trials (RCTs).  • Insight into patient recruitment and retention strategies.  • Knowledge of the regulatory aspects of conducting human subjects research, including how to apply the principles of the Belmont Report and HIPAA compliance. column6: WHO WE ARE:  At Optimum Health Physical Therapy, our mission is to provide exceptional, patient-centered care that promotes healing, restores function, and enhances overall well-being. We are dedicated to utilizing evidence-based treatments and personalized rehabilitation plans to help our patients achieve their optimal physical health. Our team of experienced therapists is committed to empowering individuals through education, movement, and hands-on therapy, ensuring a faster and more effective recovery. Supporting Therapists – Assisting physical therapists with non-clinical tasks, such as positioning patients or demonstrating simple exercises.  6. Monitoring Patients – Observing patients during therapy sessions and reporting any issues to the therapist.    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  1. Clinical Environment Exposure – You become familiar with how a physical therapy clinic operates, from patient scheduling and documentation to the use of therapeutic equipment like resistance bands, pulleys, and ultrasound machines.  5. column6: Sapna NYC is a 501c3 community-based organization that works with South Asian immigrant women and families in NYC addressing health inequities, fostering women’s empowerment, and building community power. We strive to increase access for the women in our community – access to services, access to knowledge and information, access to systems, and access to pathways for social mobility. We see ourselves as part of the community, looking to preserve the culture and community, while supporting vulnerable populations and tackling issues that push our communities into isolation, poor health, and poverty. column6: WHO WE ARE:  Loisaida Center (Loisaida, Inc.) is a community-based arts, culture, and education organization rooted in Manhattan’s Lower East Side. Our mission is to preserve, celebrate, and advance the cultural heritage of Loisaida while expanding access to the arts, community learning, and civic engagement for local residents—especially Latino, immigrant, and historically under-resourced communities. We produce year-round public programs, exhibitions, and neighborhood partnerships that strengthen community identity and build pathways to opportunity. Loisaida Center serves as a hub where community partners, artists, youth, and residents collaborate to activate public culture and community-led solutions.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  - Build and maintain a Program Operations “Open Actions” tracker (owners, due dates, status, dependencies) based on weekly staff meetings, partner meetings, and program calendars.  - Produce meeting agendas, minutes, and decision logs for internal program meetings and selected partner calls; convert notes into clear next steps within 24–48 hours.  - Create and refine standard operating procedures (SOPs) for repeat program tasks (e.g., event intake, partner onboarding, room use requests, volunteer support, A/V and space setup, bilingual signage and materials workflow, post-event wrap-up).  - Maintain a Partner Relationship Tracker (CRM-lite) in Google Sheets/Airtable that includes contact roles, program alignment, touchpoints, commitments, and follow-ups; keep it current weekly.  - Draft professional communications for partners (email follow-ups, confirmation notes, meeting recaps, “what we need from you” checklists, and timeline reminders) using Loisaida’s tone and formatting.  - Support coordination for 1–2 community-facing touchpoints per month (e.g., exhibition programming, workshops, public events, convenings): develop run-of-show drafts, staffing plans, material checklists, and post-event recap memos.  - Develop a program documentation system (folder structure, naming conventions, versioning habits, and templates) to ensure continuity across staff and cohorts.  - Produce a biweekly Program Health Brief (1–2 pages) summarizing: what shipped, upcoming deadlines, partner risks, resource gaps, and recommended actions.  - Collaborate with staff to map process bottlenecks (e.g., approvals, vendor/partner turnaround times) and propose practical improvements grounded in observed workflow.  - Complete a final capstone deliverable package and present outcomes to staff during the final week.    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  - Nonprofit program operations and coordination in a community-based arts/culture setting  - Project management fundamentals (scope, timelines, action tracking, dependency management)  - Professional meeting practice (agenda design, facilitation support, minutes, decision documentation)  - Stakeholder and partner communications (follow-ups, clarity tools, expectation-setting)  - Systems building (SOP writing, templates, workflows, documentation governance)  - Event and convening operations (run-of-show, logistics planning, post-event evaluation)  - Equity-informed, community-centered coordination practices (respectful engagement, accessibility, bilingual workflow awareness)    SUPERVISION  The intern will be supervised by the Executive & Artistic Director and/or a designated Program Lead. Supervision includes:  Weekly 30-minute 1:1 (Zoom or in-person) focused on priorities, problem-solving, professional development, and feedback on drafts.  Weekly 45-minute program team meeting to review open actions, calendar conflicts, partner updates, and near-term deliverables.  Structured onboarding (Week 1): orientation to Loisaida programs, partner landscape, current priorities, and operating tools; review of templates and examples.  Ongoing feedback: written comments on key documents (SOPs, briefs, partner emails), plus guidance on professional standards for clarity, tone, and documentation.  Resources provided: access to Loisaida’s templates, prior program materials, partner lists (as appropriate), and shared drive structure. Mandatory meetings include:  Weekly 45-minute Program Ops Meeting (scheduled during business hours)  Weekly 30-minute 1:1 Supervision (scheduled during business hours)  Occasional community events may occur outside business hours; when possible, these will be communicated in advance, and hours will be adjusted accordingly.    LOCATION:  Hybrid — Loisaida Center, 710 East 9th Street, New York, NY 10009    NOTE:  This internship is designed for students who want real responsibility and portfolio-ready outputs in operations and partnership coordination. The role is mostly independent, deadline-driven work (remote-friendly), paired with periodic on-site collaboration and community touchpoints. Interns will leave with a tangible operations toolkit (SOPs, templates, trackers, briefs) and demonstrated experience coordinating across staff and external partners in a fast-moving community organization. Onboarding is required during Week 1, and the internship culminates in a capstone deliverable package and final presentation.

column6: The mission of the Department of Records and Information Services (DORIS) is to foster a more equitable civic life by preserving and providing access to the historical and contemporary records of New York City municipal government. The Collections Management Unit of the New York City Municipal Archives seeks two CUNY interns to assist on the Archival Materials Inventory and Barcoding Project. Skills gained/outcomes:  • Learn to use Microsoft Office 365 Teams.  • Proper handling of archival/historical materials.  • Gain an understanding of what archives are and what archivists do.  • Gain an understanding of the collections stewarded by the NYC Municipal Archives that document New York City government and history dating from the 1600s to the present.  • Metadata creation and quality control.  • Assist with documenting the project and write a blog post about the project to be published on the DORIS “For the Record” blog.  • Gain teamwork experience.    Supervision and support: The student interns will be supervised by Zach Kautzman (Collections Management Archivist) and Patricia Glowinski (Collections Management Archivist). column6: About Us:  PEN America stands at the intersection of literature and human rights to protect free expression in the United States and worldwide. Our mission is to unite writers and their allies to celebrate creative expression and defend the liberties that make it possible. The candidate will develop skills and gain real-world experience in an exciting, fast-paced, and entrepreneurial environment.    PEN America’s internships offer a unique opportunity to learn more about the literary community and human rights advocacy in the United States and around the world. Communications interns are exposed to a diverse range of programming and departments, and are involved with projects that help prepare those interested in careers in marketing, public affairs, journalism, graphic design, video production, publishing, and the nonprofit sector at large. Location:  In-Person  This internship can also operate with a hybrid schedule from our headquarters in New York City, located at 120 Broadway, 26 FL North, New York, NY 10271. Writing samples include but are not limited to college papers, original essays, stories, and articles that may have been previously published, as long as they have been subject to no more than minimal editing by someone other than yourself. column5: Assistant Teacher (Intern) – Brooklyn Robot Foundry Manhattan Downtown
column6: WHO WE ARE:  Brooklyn Robot Foundry is dedicated to empowering kids aged 2 to 14 through engaging STEAM robot-building programs that ignite creativity and joy.  Located in Downtown Manhattan, our hands-on, immersive classes, full-day programs, parties, and summer sessions aim to inspire kids by teaching them the fun and excitement of STEAM learning. We believe in the DIT—do it together—mentality and building a community around fun, making things, and shaping a bright future for the next generation one robot at a time.     Check out our website to learn more:  https://brooklynrobotfoundry.com/    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  This is a part-time on-site role as an Assistant Teacher at Brooklyn Robot Foundry Manhattan Downtown in New York, NY.  When you hear the word robot, do you smile?  Do you get excited when you get to use your hands to build things?  Do you find joy in building with kids?  Do you appreciate art and science? column5: Executive Office Intern (Office of the Commissioner) - New York City Department of Records & Information Services (DORIS)
column6: WHO WE ARE:  The mission of the Department of Records and Information Services (DORIS) is to foster a more equitable civic life by preserving and providing access to the historical and contemporary records of New York City municipal government. To achieve this, the Department ensures that City records are properly maintained following professional archival and record management practices and makes materials available to diverse communities both online and in person.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  The Office of the Commissioner seeks 1 CUNY intern member to assist on a Special Project focusing on researching vital records to build a genealogical tree of individuals who were enslaved.  For this Special project: the intern would review vital records looking for data that corresponds to the names transcribed from the Archives collection of manumission records. When there is a "match" the intern will then use the vital records to build a family tree, providing a greater identity for persons, or their ancestors, who had been enslaved.     • Work alongside other interns and DORIS staff utilizing various software tools and methods used in the Special Project.   • Conduct research utilizing materials in the Municipal Library and Municipal Archives and compile this information related to this initiatives.  • Perform data entry tasks involving inputting information from various sources into an Excel spreadsheet or other software application.  • Conduct Quality Assurance to ensure entered data complies with various standards.    REQUIREMENTS/QUALIFICATIONS  *The intern should be familiar with Excel and Word  *Have an interest in City history  *Possess strong writing skills.      INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  The intern will work closely with Senior Staff on the project outlined above. The intern will learn organizational skills, working in a team, and basic management skills. The intern will also learn and improve on their existing research skills utilizing various data sources, references, and research services. The intern will learn and improve on their existing creative writing and editing skills. The intern will be using MS Office Suite applications and may work with various other apps including MS Teams, Forms, Lists, etc.     SUPERVISION:  Reporting to the Assistant Commissioner, who will supervise the CUNY intern and provide guidance and feedback. column6: ABOUT CITY PARKS FOUNDATION  City Parks Foundation (CPF) is the only independent, nonprofit organization whose mission is to offer programs in public parks throughout the five boroughs of New York City. At CPF, we are dedicated to invigorating and transforming parks into dynamic, vibrant centers of urban life through sports, arts, community development, and education programs for all New Yorkers. Our programs and community building initiatives -- located in more than 350 parks, recreation centers, and public schools across New York City -- reach 425,000 people each year.  ? We present the largest free, outdoor performing arts festival in NYC through SummerStage, presenting artists of the highest quality across multiple disciplines and genres, and marionette puppet theater in all five boroughs with our Swedish Cottage Marionette Theatre and the roving PuppetMobile.  ? Partnerships for Parks, a public-private program of City Parks Foundation and NYC Parks, supports and champions a growing network of leaders who care and advocate for the transformation of their neighborhood parks.  ? We connect youngsters to nature in the urban environment with education programs that provide learning experiences through classroom and hands-on activities in parks, urban forests, coastal areas, gardens, and recreation centers.  ? Free golf, tennis, track & field, soccer, and fitness programs bring high-quality instruction and equipment into areas where few organized athletic opportunities exist. We offer leveled training, year-round scholarship coaching, and special pro events.  Our ethos is simple: we believe thriving parks reflect thriving communities.    POSITION SUMMARY:  Learning Gardens brings year-round, field and school-based garden science learning to NYC school children and community members. Our gardens are outdoor classrooms that provide vibrant green space in some of New York City’s most densely populated neighborhoods. We operate four gardens in three boroughs. Using our four community gardens, CPF presents engaging interdisciplinary lessons to expand student learning around urban ecology, horticulture, soil science, and sustainable urban food systems. Students in 2nd – 8th grade and their teachers receive resource materials, curricula, and tools to enhance their understanding of ecosystem services and address the unique challenges of growing food in an urban environment. High School interns are trained in garden-based instruction and horticultural techniques throughout the spring and then work alongside Learning Gardens staff throughout the summer.    The Horticulture Interns will work alongside Learning Garden staff in day-to-day field operations in at least one of the Learning Gardens sites which are located in Brownsville, South Jamaica, and the South Bronx. Primary responsibilities will be to help maintain garden areas, conduct general maintenance, and provide mentorship to the existing high school Interns . Our programs and community building initiatives -- located in more than 350 parks, recreation centers, and public schools across New York City -- reach 425,000 people each year.   We present the largest free, outdoor performing arts festival in NYC through SummerStage, presenting artists of the highest quality across multiple disciplines and genres, and marionette puppet theater in all five boroughs with our Swedish Cottage Marionette Theater and the roving PuppetMobile.  Partnerships for Parks, a public-private program of City Parks Foundation and NYC Parks, supports and champions a growing network of leaders who care and advocate for the transformation of their neighborhood parks.  We connect youngsters to nature in the urban environment with education programs that provide learning experiences through classroom and hands-on activities in parks, urban forests, coastal areas, gardens, and recreation centers.  Free golf, tennis, track & field, soccer, and fitness programs bring high-quality instruction and equipment into areas where few organized athletic opportunities exist. We offer leveled training, year-round scholarship coaching, and special pro events.  Our ethos is simple: we believe thriving parks reflect thriving communities.    POSITION SUMMARY   Eco Innovators is a STEM-based internship program that supports high school students from under-resourced communities in developing environmental resilience initiatives within their schools and local communities. During their summer internship, youth will explore advocacy tools and learn techniques to tackle and help solve challenging environmental issues, including expanding green spaces, increasing recycling and reducing waste, and improving energy efficiency .    CPF has created this internship opportunity for talented college students to gain hands-on experience working with youth and explore environmental science education while helping to promote environmental stewardship, community awareness and positive youth development.     CPF is seeking a college intern for the Summer to assist the Eco Innovators Program Coordinator in providing instruction and guidance to high school interns during Mondays-Thursdays, 4 days per week for six weeks (up to 19 hours a week)  beginning July 6th, 2026 in addition to a full day orientation. WORK LOCATION:    Queensbridge Park Field House (Vernon Boulevard between the Queensboro Bridge and 41st Avenue, Queens)    QUALIFICATIONS   -Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in education, ecology, biology, environmental science, or related field OR demonstrated strong interest in environmental STEM or environmental advocacy  -Some knowledge of and interest in non-profit operations, environmental education, as well as current environmental issues and passion for socio-environmental change.  -Interest in working with a diverse team  -Willingness and ability to commit to the program schedule and times  -Willingness to explore and develop in versatility, resourcefulness and creativity

Laughing is an important part of how we communicate! We receive feedback with open arms and provide feedback with kindness and respect.    Who We Want: Individuals who are creative, active listeners, problem-solvers and interested in sharing their ideas on how to make the business grow and improve! People who enjoy working with children and/or contributing to their STEAM education. We value and celebrate a diverse and inclusive workplace. Black, Indigenous, Immigrant, Disabled, Transgender, Genderqueer, Nonbinary, People Of Color, and Neurodiverse are highly encouraged to apply.    What We Do: Brooklyn Robot Foundry introduces kids 2-14 to the magic of mechanics, creativity, and robotics. We offer super popular classes, summer sessions, birthday parties, and so much more.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  Teach robot-building classes  * Manage a classroom of kids for robot-building session  * Have an encouraging demeanor, promoting confidence in kids  * Ensure the classes stay on time, and within their agreed-upon time limit  * Troubleshoot robot issues (we will teach you how!)  * Stay positive and fun under pressure!  * Quick thinking & improvisation in the classroom  * Coordinate with other teachers, clients, and parents on site  Outside of Classes:  * Learning how to build the different projects  * Traveling to different locations to teach classes  * Keeping your tools organized and stocked  * Reporting feedback to the appropriate channels    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:    STEM Pedagogy: Learn how to teach age-appropriate engineering and robotics concepts in engaging, hands-on ways. Adapt lessons for different ages and learning styles. Encourage creativity and confidence in young learners.    Robotics, Engineering, and Circuitry: Build and troubleshoot robots using motors, switches, and circuits. Learn foundational engineering skills—no prior experience required. Safely use hand tools and light power tools.    Communication Skills: Strengthen public speaking and presentation skills. Practice breaking down complex ideas for young audiences. Communicate clearly with parents, teachers, and school staff.    Interpersonal & Teaching Skills: Develop empathy, active listening, classroom leadership, and conflict resolution. Gain experience in classroom management, mentorship, and fostering inclusive environments.    Project & Time Management: Keep lessons on track and adapt to disruptions. Learn how to manage materials, transitions, and multiple student needs at once. Plan for contingencies and dependencies.    Event Planning & Logistics: Prepare, transport, and manage materials across multiple class sites. Track inventory and supplies. Assist with set-up, break-down, and coordination of events and workshops.    Entrepreneurship, Franchising, and Small Business Operations: Get firsthand exposure to the operations of a small, mission-driven educational franchise. Learn how local businesses navigate customer service, staffing, branding, and growth strategy within a franchise model.    Navigating NYC’s Education Ecosystem & Funding Models: Understand how enrichment programs work within NYC schools, including DOE, charter, private, and PTA-funded programs. Learn about funding sources such as POs, grants, scholarships, and third-party programs like Bright Horizons. Observe program development, pricing, and proposal processes. Support programs designed to reach underserved communities.    SUPERVISION    Interns will receive close, consistent supervision and support throughout their placement. Ongoing supervision includes regular check-ins, feedback sessions, and access to mentors on-site. Interns are never placed alone in a classroom until/unless they are confident and prepared, and there is always an experienced staff member present for guidance. Interns are gradually given more responsibility as they gain confidence and competency, with feedback and support provided at every stage. Weekend opportunities are also possible. Exact days/times will depend on the intern’s availability and the current class schedule. Occasional mandatory training, staff meetings, or special events may occur during daytime hours and will be communicated in advance.    LOCATION    Mode: In-Person  Interns will travel to class sites at schools and enrichment centers throughout Brooklyn and Queens. Exact locations vary by week and program partner.    Supervisor Office location: 75 Scott Avenue Brooklyn, NY, 11237    NOTE    This is an in-person position with variable teaching locations. column5: Tech Interns – CUNY Tech Prep
column6: About CUNY Tech Prep  In Fall 2015, the CUNY Institute for Software Design and Development, in collaboration with the NYC Tech Talent Pipeline, launched CUNY Tech Prep (CTP), a year long technical and professional development program for CUNY computer science majors to learn in-demand technologies, master professional soft skills, and land great tech jobs in NYC. CTP Hacks:  - Coordinate both virtual and in-person elements of CTP Hacks to ensure a seamless experience for fellows, mentors, and judges.  - Set up event physical and virtual venues to support fellows’ project hacking experience.   - Build and update the CTP Hacks website with clear, engaging, and timely information.  - Administer the Slack workspace, facilitating team formation, encouraging interaction, and resolving technical issues.  - Manage the DevPost platform, ensuring participants can submit projects and access event details with ease.  - Onboard mentors and judges by preparing materials, managing access, and fielding  questions about hackathon rules, team challenges, and ad hoc issues.  - Troubleshoot event-day challenges to keep activities running smoothly.  - Mentor participants, as needed, in project ideation, coding, debugging, and pitching.  2. column5: 3D Design + Print-Ready Engineering Intern– CtrlAltX Studios
column6: Job Type: Remote  Program Dates: July 13, 2026 – August 21, 2026 (set by program)  Time Commitment: 19 hours/week during typical business hours (Mon–Fri)  Compensation: Paid internship (paid by the Research Foundation of CUNY (RF) as agreed)    About CtrlAltX Studios    CtrlAltX Studios is a creative technology studio and product lab building at the intersection of design, fabrication, and modern creator culture. We prototype and produce premium physical products and limited drops using 3D printing and a 40W laser for engraving/cutting, with strong aesthetics and real manufacturability.    Role Summary    You will design production-ready 3D models that can go directly into printing and (when applicable) laser engraving workflows. Printing/fabrication happen in-studio; you support end-to-end remotely from design through “release-ready” QC packages.    Key Responsibilities   - Create original CAD/3D models for functional objects, product components, and branded items   - Translate requirements into manufacturable geometry (clean topology, correct scale, strength)   - Engineer for print success: orientation, supports strategy, wall thickness, overhangs, tolerance/fit   - Prepare release packages: STL + source files + print notes + QC checklist + version logs   - Preferred (laser-ready): create/clean engraving vectors (SVG/DXF/PDF), plan engraving placement, and propose jig/alignment concepts for repeatability    Deliverables   - Print-ready STL + editable source file (STEP/F3D/BLEND/etc.)   - Print notes (orientation, supports, tolerances, risk notes)   - QC checklist + revision notes   - If laser-related: engraving/cut files (SVG/DXF/PDF) + placement/alignment notes    Supervision + Meetings   - 2x/week standing meetings (planning + review)   - Additional meetings as needed for urgent reviews, clarifications, or release approvals   - Work is remote and async-friendly, but deadlines and documentation quality matter    Required Application Materials (Portfolio/Artifacts)   - Provide one link (portfolio/Drive/PDF) with 3–6 examples:   - At least 2 print-ready designs (not just renders) with screenshots   - At least 1 example with short DFM notes (orientation/supports/wall thickness/tolerances)   - Preferred: STL + source file sample for one model   - Bonus (preferred): engraving-ready vector example (SVG/DXF/PDF) or jig/alignment concept    Example CtrlAltX Projects   - Branded accessories (tags, desk objects, plates, charms)   - column5: Patent Radar Research + Feature Risk Intern – CtrlAltX Studios
column6: Job Type: Remote  Program Dates: July 13, 2026 – August 21, 2026 (set by program)  Time Commitment: 19 hours/week during typical business hours (Mon–Fri)  Compensation: Paid internship (paid by the Research Foundation of CUNY (RF) as agreed)    About CtrlAltX Studios    CtrlAltX Studios builds new product concepts across physical goods and creative tech. We move fast, but we take IP seriously. “Patent Radar” is our internal system for early prior-art awareness so we can design smarter and reduce avoidable risk without slowing innovation.    Role Summary    You will conduct structured patent and prior-art research, map findings to feature proposals, and write clear, repeatable Feature Risk Briefs that support internal decision-making.  Important: this is research support only—not legal advice.    Key Responsibilities  - Run structured searches using credible sources (e.g., Google Patents + official patent databases)  - Identify potentially relevant patents/prior art for product features and workflows  - Translate findings into plain English: what it likely covers, why it might matter, confidence level  - Categorize results: Likely Relevant / Possibly Relevant / Not Relevant  - Maintain clean research logs (links, search terms, dates, notes) for repeatability  - Suggest conceptual design-around directions (non-legal) to support innovation    Deliverables  - Weekly Patent Radar update (new findings + top items + changes)  - 1–2 page Feature Risk Briefs (structured and consistent)  - Final “IP Heatmap” + watchlist recommendations    Supervision + Meetings  - 2x/week standing meetings (priorities + review of briefs)  - Additional meetings as needed for new feature intake, high-priority risk flags, or deep dives    You must maintain a clean audit trail and consistent brief structure    Required Application Materials (Artifact Instead of Portfolio)  - Submit one 1–2 page mini research brief (PDF/Doc link):    Option A (preferred): pick a product feature (real or hypothetical), find 2 patents or credible prior-art sources, and include:  - what each covers (plain English)  - why it might be relevant  - confidence level  - recommended next step (ignore/monitor/deeper research)  - links + search terms used    Option B: translate a patent claim into plain English and propose 2–3 conceptual design-arounds.  Do not write legal conclusions (“this infringes”).    Example CtrlAltX Projects  - IP scans for physical product concepts (accessories, modular parts, engraved items)  - Workflow scans: “design ? print ? engrave ? QC ? release”  - Building a Patent Radar playbook: query library + logging standards + brief templates

column5: DUPLICATE - Forest Restoration Intern – NYC Parks, Natural Areas Management Team

column5: Bronx Summer Institute Administrative Intern - Sadie Nash Leadership Project
column6: WHO ARE WE  Sadie Nash Leadership Project provides award-winning, experiential social justice education to more than 500 young women and gender-expansive youth of color each year in New York City and Newark, NJ. Operating with love and rigor, we use the tools of popular education to build critical consciousness, community, and college readiness. We strengthen, empower, and equip participants to lead lives rooted in joy, liberation, and collective care.    Our flagship program, Summer Institute (SI), is an immersive six-week experience for high school students. Nashers explore leadership, feminism, and social justice through classes, workshops, field trips, and intimate conversations with community leaders. Participants engage with concepts of power, identity, and privilege, developing the skills to critically analyze their lived experiences within broader social and political contexts through project-based learning. SI operates at five in-person sites: Manhattan, Queens, The Bronx, Brooklyn, and Newark, NJ.     INTERNSHIP OVERVIEW  We are seeking energetic and passionate Administrative Interns to support our summer program at five in-person sites. Interns are on site at each location supporting the teaching staff with a range of administrative tasks. They act as program and operations support staff ensuring that staff and our young people have everything they need to run a successful program. This role offers hands-on experience in using technology tools for administrative support, project management skill building, financial reporting and tracking and low stakes engagement with our young people. Interns who are selected are expected to attend training prior to the start of their role during the week of June 22, 2026.      WHAT YOU’LL DO    Documentation and Reporting- Interns will lead most of the administrative work for the summer location they are assigned to. This includes supporting participant documentation & database, digitizing organizational paperwork & documents, processing expenditures including check requests and supply requests.    Day-to-Day Programming Tasks- Interns are responsible for any administrative tasks that may arise daily, this includes but is not limited to supporting large event gatherings & chaperoning student field trips and picking up & transporting program supplies across sites.    WHO YOU ARE & KEYS TO SUCCESS (THE MUST-HAVES)    All-Hands-On-Deck Mentality: Interns approach every task—with the same energy as their own personal work—whether it’s prepping name tags, moving furniture, or transferring supplies. This high-energy, hands-on role requires significant “sweat equity,” as a large portion of time is devoted to the practical, behind-the-scenes tasks that make our programs run smoothly.    Social Justice Alignment: Interns are excited about putting SNLP's mission and goals into practice. This includes a commitment to and grounding in intersectional feminism, racial and gender equity, LGBTQIA+ rights, as well as learning and utilizing restorative practices.    Intern will learn/develop:  - Project Management and Coordination  - Administrative Support/Non-profit Management  - Leadership and Social Justice Frameworks    Work Schedule:  - DAYS/TIME: Monday-Wednesday 9:30am-4:00pm daily     - LOCATION: Interns are expected to be in-person at their assigned location for the entirety of their schedule. We do our best to assign interns to the closest location to them but cannot guarantee placement. In NYC: Manhattan, Queens, Bronx and Brooklyn. In NJ: Newark, NJ (Business district).    Interview Questions  1) What draws you to Sadie Nash’s mission?   2) What is something you’re hoping to get out of your time with us?  3) Share a time when you completed a big project. What did you find challenging? What were you proud of?  4) How do you keep yourself accountable to your tasks and deadlines?  5) Please share anything else you’d like us to know about you.

column6: Position/Title: Catalyst Community Organizing Internship    Start Date:   End Date:   Compensation:   Employment Type: P/T Seasonal   ABOUT CITY PARKS FOUNDATION   City Parks Foundation (CPF) is the only independent, nonprofit organization whose mission is to offer programs in public parks throughout the five boroughs of New York City. column6: WHO WE ARE:  The Natural Resources Group, within NYC Parks, manages over 12,500 acres of natural areas across NYC, including forests, wetlands, and grasslands, focused on improving the health of these natural areas. Working under the guidance and oversight of various NYC Parks Ecologists, interns may engage in tasks pertaining to native and introduced plant identification, vegetation and wildlife monitoring and social survey interviews of park attendees. Interns may be responsible for providing technical and field assistance in natural areas monitoring and restoration projects, such as:      Vegetation monitoring: e.g. measuring size and health of plant species to assess restoration outcomes     Wildlife monitoring: e.g. collecting data on amphibian, fish, mammal, bird populations in forests and wetlands      Assisting in data entry, data cleaning, and data analysis of ongoing monitoring projects     Assist in conducting interviews with park visitors and collecting observational data on park usage     Assist in invertebrate identification relating to the Emerald Ash Borer biocontrol monitoring project     Interact with staff and the public in a courteous and professional manner.     INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  Introduction to the environmental field through ecological hands-on field work      Field identification of flora and fauna in the local New York City region     Introduction to laboratory work, including safety guidelines on ethanol use and proficiency in microscopy     Professional development including near-peer mentorship opportunities and career-readiness     Introduction to data collection, data cleaning, and analysis     Proficiency with Microsoft Suites     SUPERVISION  CUNY Career Launch interns will be supervised by Natural Resources Training Coordinator and Research & Monitoring Ecologist/Staff. column5: Research Assistant – Behavioral Neuroscience and Martial Arts Analysis
column6: WHO WE ARE:    The Alvarado Lab at Queens College (CUNY) investigates how behavior and decision-making are shaped by physical form, social context, and environmental cues. We work at the intersection of neuroscience, ethology, and integrative biology, with research spanning both animal and human systems. Our current focus includes understanding strategic behavior in martial arts through detailed analysis of body movement and decision-making under pressure. The lab is deeply committed to undergraduate training and hands-on research, especially for students interested in careers in behavioral neuroscience, clinical psychology, or behavioral ecology.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:    1. Use BORIS (Behavioral Observation Research Interactive Software) to manually score and annotate martial arts video footage    2. Apply a predefined ethogram to identify and categorize actions (e.g., throws, feints, grip changes, repositioning)    3. Help identify emergent patterns in strategic behavior based on movement sequences and context    4. Collaborate with team members to refine behavioral coding schemes and validate inter-rater reliability    5. Participate in weekly lab meetings and contribute to discussions on behavioral theory and observational rigor    6. Support ongoing research that began in Summer 2025    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:    1. Ethogram design and behavioral coding techniques used in human and animal behavior research    2. Observational research methodology and video-based behavioral analysis    3. Concepts in ethology, social cognition, and behavioral neuroscience    4. Strategies for pattern recognition, hypothesis development, and theory building    5. Skills in documenting behavior with high accuracy and consistency    6. Scientific teamwork and presentation skills within a research team    SUPERVISION:    Interns will work closely with senior undergraduate researchers and graduate students who specialize in behavioral analysis, with direct mentorship from project leads. Dr. Sebastian Alvarado will provide oversight, conceptual framing, and guidance during lab meetings. Interns will receive regular check-ins and feedback on scoring accuracy, interpretation, and theoretical grounding. This position is ideal for students interested in human psychology, behavioral neuroscience, ethology, or clinical/observational research.    2. Preference will be given to applicants with prior martial arts experience, especially in sports such as Judo, BJJ, Karate, or Wrestling.    3. This project does not require programming or computer science skills, but rather a sharp eye for detail and interest in behavior and strategy.    4. Onboarding and training with BORIS and the ethogram will be provided at the start of the internship.

column5: Social Media Intern - BK ROT
column6: WHO WE ARE:  BK ROT is a food waste hauling and composting service powered by youth and young adults who are employed to collect food waste by bike and maintain compost processing sites. The service operates within North Brooklyn and works to increase composting at the neighborhood level. We provide locally sourced and produced compost within our community in support of food justice and soil building projects.     We are seeking a creative and energetic Social Media Intern to amplify BK ROT’s story and engage our online community. We are looking for an individual who is comfortable being a member of a team and who can take initiative independently. The ability to multitask, while maintaining a consistent brand voice, is essential in this position. The ideal candidate for this job is resourceful, visually oriented, highly organized, and accountable to their work, both in-person and remote. Assuring a steady and timely flow of content creation with transparency and strong communication is key to success in this position.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  - Develop and schedule engaging content (photos, videos, graphics, and stories) for BK ROT’s social media platforms (Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, etc.).  - Attend weekly collections and site workdays to capture authentic, real-time content of the team and operations in action.  - Assist in creating promotional materials for events, fundraisers, and the annual Youth Leaders Program culminating event.  - Synthesize complex information about composting, food justice, and climate justice into accessible and compelling social media posts  - Monitor and respond to comments/DMs to build an active online community.  - Collaborate with partners for cross-promotion and coordinate content calendars with outreach events.  - Track insights to report on engagement and refine content strategy.  - Research trending topics and hashtags to increase visibility.    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  - How to plan, create, and schedule content that aligns with an organization's mission and campaign goals.  - How to translate on-the-ground impact (composting, youth jobs) into compelling visual narratives for different platforms.  - Best practices for engaging an online audience, responding to comments, and building community.  - How to track engagement metrics, analyze performance data, and adjust strategy accordingly.  - How to maintain a consistent tone and visual identity across multiple channels while advocating for environmental justice.    SUPERVISION  This position will report to the Program Manager. BK ROT uses a collaborative model where the intern will have opportunity to engage and learn from peers. BK ROT will offer mentorship and training resources to best support the interns success.    WORK SCHEDULE:  Most work is done between hours of 9am and 5pm.     LOCATION:  Hybrid

column5: AI & Data Science Interns
column6: ## About Cambio Labs    Cambio Labs is a NYC-based nonprofit building community infrastructure through technology. We design AI-powered platforms that help low-income entrepreneurs and workforce learners access practical, wealth-building education.    We are evolving our platform, **Journey**, into a Platform-as-a-Product (PaaP) model powered by intelligent systems, including **Sparky**, our AI coaching assistant.    ---    As an **AI & Data Science Intern**, you will help architect, test, and optimize real AI systems used by thousands of learners across NYC public housing and workforce programs.    You will work directly on:    - LLM-powered coaching systems  - Adaptive learning algorithms  - Career pathway matching models  - AI-assisted grant writing tools  - Data pipelines that inform product strategy    This is ideal for students who:    - Build projects outside of class  - Experiment with LLMs, APIs, and automation  - Want real product ownership  - Care about equity + applied AI    ## What You’ll Work On    ### 1. AI Systems Development    - Improve and expand Sparky (LLM-powered AI coach)  - Build and test prompt pipelines + retrieval workflows (RAG systems)  - Develop adaptive logic for personalized learning paths  - Analyze behavioral and engagement data to improve AI decision-making  - Implement NLP-based feedback systems  - Evaluate model performance + iterate    ### 2. Applied Data Science    - Build dashboards to track learner outcomes  - Conduct exploratory data analysis on participant engagement + skill growth  - Design lightweight predictive models (e.g., retention, completion likelihood)  - Help design ethical AI use guidelines for low-income communities    ### 3. Product Strategy + Platform Innovation    - Support our shift to Platform-as-a-Product  - Research AI trends in ed-tech and workforce tech  - Help define product features based on real user data  - Contribute to go-to-market materials grounded in technical reality    ## What We’re Looking For    **Required**    - CUNY junior or senior  - Major in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Applied Math, or related field  - Strong Python proficiency  - Familiarity with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) OR strong interest in learning  - Experience working with data (pandas, SQL, visualization tools)  - Ability to think both technically and strategically    **Bonus**    - Experience with RAG systems  - Experience with LangChain, vector databases, embeddings  - ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn)  - Experience deploying small applications  - Interest in AI ethics or public-interest technology    ## What You’ll Gain    - Real-world AI system building  - Ownership over product features used by real communities  - Exposure to nonprofit + venture-adjacent product strategy  - Portfolio-ready work (with measurable impact)  - Close mentorship from senior leadership  - Strong letters of recommendation  - Potential pathway to paid extended role or employment    ## Why This Role Is Different    Most internships simulate impact.    This one creates it.    You will help build AI tools that:    - Support first-generation entrepreneurs  - Help public housing residents build businesses  - Make workforce education practical + adaptive    We are building community infrastructure, and AI is a core layer. If you want to build serious AI systems that matter, this is for you.

column5: Urban Wildlife Research & Conservation Intern – Urban Wildlife Alliance
column6: WHO WE ARE:  Urban Wildlife Alliance is a nonprofit based in New York City, dedicated to compassionate conservation, wildlife rehabilitation, and advocacy. We work at the intersection of science, ethics, and public policy to promote the welfare of urban wildlife. Through partnerships with institutions like NYU, we are conducting research to understand and address the root causes of the urban wildlife crisis in city environments. We advocate for humane, science-based solutions that foster a more sustainable and inclusive future for both animals and humans.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  • Conduct literature reviews and background research  • Enter, analyze, and synthesize data from academic research and city planning sources  • Support the collection and organization of research data using spreadsheets or other tools  • Help develop recommendations for wildlife-conscious policies and infrastructure  • Collaborate on internal presentations and advocacy documents  • Participate in regular check-ins and team meetings    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  • Urban ecology and wildlife conservation science  • Research methods and policy analysis  • Data entry and analysis for real-world environmental and policy research  • Critical thinking and real-world problem-solving  • Professional communication and collaborative skills  • Advocacy techniques grounded in research and compassion    SUPERVISION:  Interns will be supervised directly by the Executive Director of Urban Wildlife Alliance, with support from research collaborators and project leads. They will receive regular feedback, attend scheduled check-ins, and have access to ongoing mentorship and support throughout the internship.    REQUIREMENTS:  • Interest in wildlife conservation, urban sustainability, or environmental justice  • Dependability and availability for initial training and regular weekday meetings (between 9–5)  • Research and analytical skills; ability to read and summarize scientific and planning documents  • Clear written and verbal communication  • Comfort with remote work and collaboration via Zoom and Google Workspace    WORK SCHEDULE:  Flexible schedule, but interns must be available for Zoom meetings during weekdays between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM ET. This position is mostly remote, but optional in-person events or site visits may be offered with advance notice. Onboarding and training sessions will take place at the beginning of the internship.    LOCATION:  Virtual    NOTE:  This internship is a unique opportunity to explore the emerging field of urban wildlife research and policy, with real-world applications in city planning, public health, environmental justice, and sustainable development. You'll join a collaborative team working on current and future projects that may include:    • A joint research study with NYU investigating the root causes of wildlife injuries and illnesses in New York City  • A policy review of environmental impact assessments and infrastructure projects in NYC to identify where wildlife welfare is overlooked or neglected  • An analysis of green space planning and urban park development to assess their suitability as functioning ecosystems for birds, mammals, and invertebrates  • Literature reviews, stakeholder mapping, and data synthesis to inform wildlife-friendly policy recommendations  • Review of international urban wildlife conservation projects and initiatives.  • Analysis of urban wildlife protection rules and regulations.    This internship is ideal for students interested in environmental science, sustainability, urban planning, public policy, ecology, animal welfare, or conservation biology.

column6: WHO WE ARE:  Anew Material is a NYC startup creating plant-based materials to replace petrochemical ingredients used in consumer products. column6: About Us:  The YWCA of the City of New York (YW-NYC) is on a mission to eliminate racism, empower women and promote peace, justice, freedom and dignity for all. We are a social justice organization dedicated to addressing issues that emerge at the intersection of race, class and gender. Founded in 1858, the YW- NYC is the first YW in the United States and part of an international movement of YWs worldwide. We currently serve 1,500 New York City school children by providing leadership and advocacy training for young women through our high school Girls Initiatives and Out-of-School Time (OST) programs for elementary and middle school students in diverse communities in Manhattan and Brooklyn.    Responsibilities:  • Provide administrative support including document filing, photocopying, scanning, data entry, and organizing program materials.  • Monitor, track, and update inventory of supplies; support with ordering and restocking of materials as needed.  • Contribute to program planning by supporting activity preparation and ensuring activity readiness by preparing daily materials and resources in accordance with lesson plans and scheduled activities.  • Help with attendance tracking, daily sign-in/out procedures and data entry.  • Support special events, field trips, and family engagement activities as needed.  • Organize program materials and maintain orderly storage areas.  • Assist with student supervision during summer afterschool activities, transitions, and dismissal.  • Perform other duties as assigned to support the success of the program.    Intern Will Learn/Develop:  • Practical experience in youth program operations and education-based community work.  • Project management and organizational skills through planning and supporting daily program activities.  • Administrative and data management skills, including attendance tracking and inventory management.  • Communication and teamwork skills through collaboration with staff, families, and students.  • Leadership and behavior management techniques for engaging with children in group settings.  • Event coordination and logistics, including preparation and support for trips and special events.  • An understanding of nonprofit program management, and compliance requirements    Supervision:  • Interns will be supervised by a Site Program Director and/or Assistant Program Director who will provide regular guidance and mentorship.  • Bi-weekly supervision meetings will be held to review progress, set goals, and provide feedback.  • Interns will receive on-site training in program procedures, safety protocols, and youth engagement strategies.  • Supervisors will offer ongoing support through informal check-ins, professional development opportunities, and structured evaluations at the mid-point and end of the internship.  • Interns will have access to program resources, administrative tools, and collaborative support from experienced YWCA staff.    Requirements  • Currently enrolled students; preferred fields of study include Education, Child Development, Social Work, Psychology, or related fields.  • Prior experience working with children or in a youth program is strongly preferred, but not required.  • Strong organizational and administrative skills  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and comfort with basic data entry and record- keeping.  • Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate effectively with students, families, and staff.  • Dependable, punctual, and able to take initiative while working both independently and as part of a team.  • Comfortable supervising and engaging with groups of children in a structured program environment.  • Physical ability to remain active during student activities, set up program spaces, and lift/move light supplies (up to 20 lbs).  • Positive, flexible, and professional attitude with a commitment to youth development.  • Must successfully complete background check and required DOE and DOH clearances. column6: The Center for Justice Innovation’s (the Center) Data Analytics and Applied Research (DAAR) department advances the Center’s mission by harnessing the power of data to drive meaningful changes in systems and communities. DAAR collaborates with internal departments and external stakeholders to develop, implement, and evaluate data-driven programs, policies, and practices that address real-world justice challenges. DAAR routinely undertakes research to enhance the operation of the Center’s operating sites and is currently conducting multiple research projects on topics such as the efficacy of misdemeanor mental health courts, the benefits of rapid engagement in diversion programming, and the impact of warrants on case outcomes. The supervisor will assign projects to the intern, set deadlines, and provide feedback on the intern’s work. The two will meet at least once weekly for an hour to discuss progress on assigned projects and the internship experience and will be in regular communication in the office and over email, phone, and Slack.    DAAR is committed to providing a robust and supportive internship experience. Along with the supervision discussed above, the supervisor will ensure that the intern collaborates with other staff members, is included in all relevant research team meetings and trainings, and has regular opportunities to learn about applied research and the larger mission of the Center for Justice Innovation. Ideal candidate will be a detail oriented self-starting individual enrolled in a degree program in computer science, data science, mechanical or electrical engineering, or a related field who can demonstrate ability to execute the project and have proficiency in Python, Ubuntu, PostgeSQL, and other computer software see section 3.2 in https://tools4cities-wiki.readthedocs.io/en/latest/citylayers/architecture/index.html#) and the attachment for more information on base deployment of the platform.     Students will be working either remotely or in a hybrid (remote and in office). The company is headquartered in Great Neck, New York, with additional offices in Manhattan.  M&R is certified to manage selected brands of Marriott International, Hilton Worldwide, Hyatt Hotels Corporation, InterContinental Hotels Group, Choice Hotels International, Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, and Best Western Hotels & Resorts. Guest Service & Front Desk Operations  • Greet and welcome guests in a professional and friendly manner  • Assist with guest check-in and check-out procedures  • Respond to guest inquiries, requests, and concerns promptly  • Maintain a positive and service-oriented attitude at all times  Reservations & Systems Support  • Learn to navigate the Property Management System (PMS)  • Assist with room assignments and reservation updates  • Support accuracy of guest profiles and billing information  Communication & Coordination  • Communicate effectively with Housekeeping, Engineering, and other departments  • Assist in resolving guest service issues in coordination with supervisors  • Support daily shift reports and documentation  Administrative & Operational Support  • Assist with front office administrative tasks  • Support daily audit preparation when applicable  • Participate in team meetings and training sessions  INTERN WILL LEARN / DEVELOP  This internship provides hands-on experience in:  • Front Office operations within a branded hotel environment  • Guest service excellence and service recovery techniques  • Property Management System functionality  • Interdepartmental communication and teamwork  • Hospitality professionalism and operational standards  Interns will gain real-world experience in hotel operations while developing strong communication, problem-solving, and customer service skills. Description  This Internship provides students with hands-on experience in Woodhull’s Nursing Education Department, offering a behind-the-scenes look at how clinical education and nursing professional development work together to support patient care. Interns will gain operational, organizational, and communication skills while assisting staff, assisting in managing daily operations, documentation, and record-keeping. This role is highly staff-facing with staff interaction, making it ideal for those interested in healthcare administration, hospital operations, and gaining exposure to processes focused on improving patient outcomes thorough staff engagement in the learning and the process of developing critical thinking skills.    Responsibilities  As a Intern, you will:  • Monitor and regularly replenish the inventory of administrative and some medical supplies.  Organize and maintain supplies inventory, gaining skills in inventory management.  • Ensuring productive workflow by managing departmental forms. Ensuring that all forms are in stock and available. Qualifications & Skills  • Proficiency in MS Word and basic office software.  • Strong professionalism and ability to work in a hospital setting.  • Excellent communication skills to interact with staff and visitors.  • Empathy and compassion in a patient-care environment.  • Ability to apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills.  • Emotional intelligence and awareness of patient and staff needs.  • Highly detail-oriented and organized.  • Strong time management skills to handle multiple responsibilities.  • Ability to work collaboratively with healthcare teams. column5: RISK MANAGEMENT (BEHAVIORAL HEALTH & PSYCHIATRY), ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT INTERN -NYC HEALTH + HOSPITALS / WOODHULL HOSPITAL
column6: WHO WE ARE: NYC Health + Hospitals/ Woodhull is the hospital of choice for residents of North Brooklyn, including Bushwick, Williamsburg, Greenpoint, Bedford-Stuyvesant, and Fort Greene communities. Providing both clinical and non-clinical career paths that work to support positive outcomes and experiences for our patients and community. Woodhull’s goal is to provide real-world working experiences to up-and-coming healthcare professionals.     Description: Risk management in healthcare involves a comprehensive system of clinical and administrative processes designed to detect, assess, mitigate, and prevent risks to patients, staff, and the organization. We work to identify the root causes and develop sustainable actions to prevent recurrence for patients, staff, and the hospital; without one, we cannot strive. As a Risk Management Administrative Assistant Intern, you will support critical functions of the department, ensuring proper documentation, communication, and risk assessment tracking. This internship provides a unique opportunity to develop administrative, analytical, and organizational skills in a healthcare setting.    Responsibilities  As an intern, your responsibilities include, but are not limited to:  • Meeting Support: Assisting in team meetings by taking and transcribing meeting minutes.  • Office Equipment & Software Operations: Utilizing computers, telephones, copiers, overhead paging systems, and other communication devices.  • Document Management: Typing, reviewing, proofreading, and editing a variety of materials, including reports, emails, meeting minutes, and charts.  • Records & File Organization: Organizing and maintaining departmental files, records, and tracking logs.  • Call & Inquiry Handling: Receiving and directing incoming calls, recording messages, and ensuring timely communication with the appropriate parties.  • Data Tracking & Reporting: Assisting in maintaining departmental tracking logs and preparing data for analysis.  • Confidentiality & Compliance: Ensuring the security and confidentiality of all patient, staff, and risk management-related documents.  • Real-World Experience: Gaining hands-on administrative experience in risk management within a healthcare setting.    Requirements  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel (formulas, tables, graphs, pivot tables), Word, and PowerPoint.  • Strong research skills (preferred but not required).  • Excellent communication skills (both written and verbal).  • Strong organizational and time management skills.  • Attention to detail and accuracy in documentation.  • Ability to apply critical thinking and problem-solving techniques.  • Understanding of basic statistics and data analysis.  • Strong sense of professionalism and ability to maintain confidentiality.  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team setting.  • Customer service skills and ability to interact professionally with staff at all levels.  • Keyboarding and data entry skills.    Recommended Majors  This internship is ideal for students majoring in Healthcare Administration, Risk Management, Business Administration, Psychiatry, Neuroscience, Public Health, Statistics, or Legal Studies.    Available: Monday through Friday, Schedules (day shift only); Shift Start Time 10:00 am; in-person opportunity only    Location:     760 Broadway, Brooklyn, NY    NOTE:   IF SELECTED FOR CONSIDERATION, WOODHULL VOLUNTEER SERVICES WILL REACH OUT TO APPLICANTS TO SCHEDULE AN INTERVIEW.  NOTE:    SHOULD STUDENT ACCEPT AN OFFER TO INTERN AT WOODHULL HOSPITAL, ONBOARDING WILL BE REQUIRED

column5: Community Engagement Intern, WholeYouNYC Social Care Network - Public Health Solutions
column6: Organization Description  Public Health Solutions (PHS) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to improving health equity and addressing health-related social needs (HRSN) for historically underserved communities across New York City. As the largest public health nonprofit serving NYC, PHS has worked for over 70 years to bridge healthcare and community services to improve health outcomes.  PHS leads WholeYouNYC, a Social Care Network (SCN) funded by the New York State Department of Health to serve Medicaid members in Brooklyn, Manhattan, and Queens. The network consists of more than 200 healthcare providers and community-based organizations and connects eligible Medicaid members to food and nutrition support, housing assistance, transportation, and other critical services that address the social drivers of health. This Social Care Network Impacts thousands of lives through coordinated community partnerships and referrals and generating millions of dollars in estimated healthcare savings.  The Community Engagement Team (CET) plays a critical role in driving awareness of the Social Care Network and supporting Medicaid members in completing health-related social needs screenings.  ________________________________________    Program Description  The Community Engagement Team (CET) is responsible for:  • Promoting the WholeYouNYC Social Care Network across Brooklyn, Manhattan, and Queens  • Supporting Medicaid members in completing the state-required health-related social needs self-screening tool  • Coordinating and participating in community events and partner engagements  • Activating healthcare and community-based organizations to support screenings  • Tracking outreach metrics and improving real-time screening outcomes    CET works closely with internal teams including Network Performance, Quality Improvement, Marketing & Communications, and Managed Care Plan partners.  ________________________________________    Position Summary  The Community Engagement Team (CET) is seeking motivated, community-oriented interns to support outreach, event coordination, and screening promotion efforts within the WholeYouNYC Social Care Network (SCN).  Interns will work closely with CET Managers and Specialists to advance community-based engagement strategies that connect Medicaid members to essential health-related social services. This role offers a dynamic blend of field-based outreach and programmatic support, providing hands-on experience in public health implementation, health equity initiatives, and large-scale systems transformation.  As a Community Engagement Intern, you will contribute directly to expanding access to services for underserved New Yorkers while gaining exposure to cross-sector collaboration among community-based organizations, healthcare providers, and managed care plans. This is an opportunity to support a statewide Medicaid initiative while developing professional skills in community engagement, communications, and public health operations.    What You’ll Do  Intern responsibilities may include:  Community Outreach Support  • Assist CET staff at community events, resource fairs, and neighborhood gatherings  • Support real-time member engagement efforts and help guide Medicaid members through the self-screening process  • Distribute educational materials and explain program eligibility and available services    Event & Convening Support  • Assist with planning and logistics for CET-led events  • Support coordination of partner convenings and community-based events  • Help manage event tracking, attendance documentation, and follow-up communications    Partner Engagement Support  • Update and maintain partner contact trackers and outreach lists  • Assist in preparing materials for meetings with community-based organizations and healthcare partners  • Support follow-up communications after outreach activities and partner engagements    Data & Tracking  • Support tracking of weekly screening and outreach metrics  • Assist with compiling outreach activity reports  • Help monitor community engagement performance indicators to inform strategy    What You’ll Gain  • Real-world public health systems experience  • Exposure to Medicaid and social care reform initiatives  • Experience in stakeholder engagement and cross-sector collaboration  • Professional mentorship from public health leaders  • Skills in outreach strategy, communications, and operational coordination  ________________________________________    What We’re Looking For  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills  • Interest in public health, health equity, or community engagement  • Organized and detail-oriented  • Comfortable engaging with diverse populations  • Ability to work in both virtual and in-person environments  • Bilingual fluency preferred  ________________________________________    Who Should Apply?  CUNY students who are:  • Interested in public health, healthcare access, or social services  • Passionate about working with underserved communities  • Excited about hands-on field experience  • Interested in nonprofit or health systems careers    Work Schedule:  Monday - Friday 9am-5pm    Location:  40 Worth St, 4th Fl, New York, NY 10013

column6: WHO WE ARE:  At Essen Health Care, we care for that!    As the largest privately held multispecialty medical group in the Bronx, we provide high-quality, compassionate, and accessible medical care to some of the most vulnerable and under-served residents of New York State.
