column6: Who We Are:    The Center for Justice Innovation’s Data Analytics and Applied Research (DAAR) department advances the Center’s mission by harnessing the power of data to drive meaningful changes in systems and communities. DAAR works with program and operational teams to ensure that data collected through case management systems (CMS) is accurate, usable, and aligned with both operational and research needs.    DAAR seeks hybrid summer interns to support projects at the intersection of data systems and applied research. This role is supervised by DAAR and may involve coordination with other departments, including technology and program staff, depending on project needs. The internship will provide hands-on experience solving real operational problems using a variety of technology platforms, while also offering insight into how program data is ultimately used for analysis, reporting, and evaluation.    Location: 520 8th Ave, New York, NY 10018; Hybrid    Responsibilities:    • Assisting with the design, testing, and refinement of data collection processes within case management systems (CMS)  • Reviewing CMS data for accuracy, completeness, and consistency, and identifying patterns or recurring data issues  • Helping translate programmatic or research needs into clear and actionable documentation  • Supporting data cleanup or documentation projects (e.g., reviewing legacy data, mapping fields, identifying duplicate or unused fields), which may involve structured data entry or data cleaning.   • Assisting with documentation related to data entry standards or internal processes  • Working across multiple platforms (e.g., CMS tools, Excel, SharePoint, survey tools, or databases) to support day-to-day data needs  • Participating in internal testing or review of system changes, as appropriate  • Supporting the development of short memos, guides, or presentations that explain data processes or findings to technical and non-technical audiences  • Participating in staff meetings, trainings, and cross-team check-ins  • Performing other duties as assigned    Supervision  The interns will be supervised by a DAAR Associate Director or their designee. The supervisor will assign projects, set deadlines, and provide feedback on the intern’s work. The intern and supervisor will meet at least once weekly to discuss progress on assigned projects and the overall internship experience, and will be in regular communication via email, Slack, and in-office check-ins.    Interns will Learn/Develop:   • Gain exposure to how case-level data flows from front-line programs into research, reporting, and evaluation  • Develop practical skills in data systems, documentation, and applied problem solving  • Learn how data infrastructure supports justice-focused programs in real operational settings  • Be included in relevant project meetings and trainings, as appropriate    Qualifications/Requirements  • Comfort working with data in some capacity — whether through coursework, research, personal projects, or prior work experience; no specific technical background is required, but candidates should be genuinely curious about data and how it's used  • Strong attention to detail and an interest in understanding how systems and processes work  • Ability to manage multiple tasks, adapt to shifting priorities, and ask questions when something is unclear  • Clear written communication skills, including an ability to explain technical concepts in plain language  • Willingness to engage with unfamiliar tools and platforms — we care more about your approach to learning new things than your existing toolkit  • Collaborative and comfortable working across teams with varying levels of technical fluency  • Interest in criminal justice reform, social services, or public interest work.    • Suggested Majors (not required — we welcome applicants from any field with relevant skills or interests)           Information Science, Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Public Policy, Sociology, Criminal Justice, Urban Studies, or a related field

column5: Social Care Navigation Intern, WholeYouNYC Social Care Network - Public Health Solutions
column6: Organization Description  Public Health Solutions (PHS) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to improving health equity and addressing health-related social needs (HRSN) for historically underserved communities across New York City. As the largest public health nonprofit serving NYC, PHS has worked for over 70 years to bridge healthcare and community services to improve health outcomes.  PHS leads WholeYouNYC, a Social Care Network (SCN) funded by the New York State Department of Health to serve Medicaid members in Brooklyn, Manhattan, and Queens. The network consists of more than 200 healthcare providers and community-based organizations and connects eligible Medicaid members to food and nutrition support, housing assistance, transportation, and other critical services that address the social drivers of health. This Social Care Network Impacts thousands of lives through coordinated community partnerships and referrals and generating millions of dollars in estimated healthcare savings.     Program Description  The Social Care Navigation team leads coordinated intake, screening, and referral operations across the WholeYouNYC Social Care Network. We connect Medicaid members to timely, equitable social care services that address health-related social needs.    Our work advances accountability, efficiency, and high-quality care coordination throughout the Social Care Network.    Position Summary   Public Health Solutions (PHS) is seeking 4 motivated and mission?driven interns to join our WholeYouNYC Social Care Navigation team. This internship offers a hands?on opportunity to support the development and growth of a citywide social care network that connects Medicaid members to essential health?related social services which includes nutrition support, housing assistance, transportation, and case management. Our goal is to reduce health disparities and improve community health outcomes.    As an intern, you will work alongside Social Care Navigators to support Medicaid members through the intake, screening, and referral process. You will help connect individuals to essential services such as food, housing, transportation, and case management, while ensuring a compassionate and member-centered experience. This role offers hands-on exposure to care coordination, community resource navigation, and the day-to-day work of advancing health equity across New York City. You will report directly to the Coordination Center Managers for the WholeYouNYC SCN and gain hands-on experience in care coordination, community resource navigation, and the delivery of social care services within a large public health network.    What You’ll Do  • Support Social Care Navigators with intake, screening, and referral activities for Medicaid members  • Conduct outreach to members by phone and/or email to assist with service connection and follow-up  • Provide accurate information about available community resources, including food, housing, transportation, and case management services  • Document member interactions and service referrals in designated systems in a timely and detailed manner  • Collaborate with Navigators and Coordination Center staff to ensure members experience smooth, person-centered support  • Assist with care coordination follow-ups to confirm successful connections to services    In addition to the responsibilities above, other opportunities and duties may be assigned.     What We’re Looking For  • Strong communication skills and a compassionate, member-centered approach  • Good organization and attention to detail, especially when documenting information  • Comfort speaking with individuals by phone and helping them understand available resources  • Interest in health equity, social determinants of health, and community-based services  • Ability to manage time effectively while balancing academic and internship responsibilities  • Willingness to learn, ask questions, and grow in a supportive team environment  • Basic familiarity with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and openness to learning new systems    Who Should Apply?  CUNY students who are:  • Interested in exploring careers in public health, social work, healthcare, or community services  • Passionate about supporting underserved communities  • Curious about how Medicaid and social care systems work in New York City  • Looking for hands-on, real-world experience in care coordination and community engagement  • Excited to make a meaningful impact while developing professional skills    Work Schedule:  Monday - Friday 9am-5pm    Location:  40 Worth St, 4th Fl, New York, NY 10013

column5: Onboarding TTA Intern, WholeYouNYC Social Care Network - Public Health Solutions
column6: About Public Health Solutions  Public Health Solutions (PHS) is a 501(c)3 non-profit community-based organization (CBO) that has existed for 70 years to improve health equity and address health-related social needs (HRSN) for historically underserved marginalized communities. As the largest public health nonprofit serving New York City, we improve health outcomes and help communities thrive by providing services directly to vulnerable families, supporting community-based organizations through our long-standing public-private partnerships, and bridging the gap between healthcare and community services. We focus on a wide range of public health issues including food and nutrition, health insurance, maternal and child health, sexual and reproductive health, tobacco control, and HIV/AIDS. Learn more about our work at healthsolutions.org.      Program Description: WholeYouNYC Social Care Network  PHS leads WholeYouNYC, a Social Care Network (SCN), funded by the New York State Department of Health, to serve Brooklyn, Manhattan, and Queens. WholeYouNYC-SCN provides access to vital Health-Related Social Needs (HRSN) services, including food and nutrition support, housing assistance, and transportation services, for over 2.3 million Medicaid members across these three boroughs, impacting thousands of lives through coordinated community partnerships and referrals and generating millions of dollars in estimated healthcare savings.   Department Description: Network Performance Team    The Onboarding Training and Technical Assistance (TTA) team at PHS leverages our extensive experience in training, stakeholder engagement, and technical assistance to onboard partners into the Social Care Network who are committed to addressing health-related social needs.     Our team is dedicated to coordinating the WholeYouNYC-SCN, facilitating collaboration between the various stakeholders across sectors that contribute to the network. In particular, our efforts include various evaluation and programmatic methods to strengthen the network and improve care delivery to Medicaid members.  The team also manages ongoing communication across the network — including weekly updates, resource coordination, and hosting office hours for both current and prospective partner organizations. Interns may gain experience in stakeholder engagement, partner communications, performance tracking, and evaluation methods. Additionally, the team collaborates with the network’s technology platform to ensure accurate tracking of overall network performance – including individual organizational performance (screenings and referrals completed, services offered, etc.) - and key performance milestones, offering interns valuable insight into data systems and impact measurement in large-scale public health initiatives.  Why This Internship Matters  If you're passionate about public health, social justice, healthcare reform, or community impact, this is your chance to work on one of New York State’s most ambitious health equity initiatives.    As an Onboarding TTA Intern, you won’t just “observe.” You’ll actively contribute to building and strengthening a Social Care Network serving 2.9 million Medicaid members across Brooklyn, Manhattan, and Queens.    This is real-world public health systems work at scale.    What You’ll Gain  • Hands-on experience in public health systems transformation  • Exposure to cross-sector collaboration (healthcare, nonprofits, government)  • Practical skills in training operations, stakeholder engagement, and data tracking  • Insight into how large-scale social care networks are built and evaluated  • Professional mentorship from leaders working at the forefront of health equity    This role is ideal for students interested in public health, nonprofit management, social work, public administration, or data-informed program operations.    Position Summary   We are seeking a driven, detail-oriented intern to support the performance and operations of the WholeYouNYC Social Care Network within the Onboarding Training and Technical Assistance team. You’ll collaborate closely with the Onboarding TTA Manager and Coordinators and report directly to the Onboarding TTA Coordinator, WholeYouNYC-SCN.    What You’ll Do  You will play a key role in strengthening onboarding and training processes that help organizations join and succeed in the Social Care Network. Responsibilities include:  • Supporting audit and data management of training records  • Assisting in tracking and disseminating learner knowledge assessments  • Contributing to the development of tools, resources, and training materials  • Supporting internal and external training communications  • Researching opportunities to strengthen network composition and impact  • Helping coordinate, schedule, and execute meetings and cross-team initiatives  You’ll see how public health reform moves from strategy to execution, and be part of making it happen.     What We’re Looking For  • Strong time management and attention to detail  • Clear and professional written and verbal communication skills  • Interest in health equity, health disparities, and health-related social needs  • Ability to collaborate effectively in virtual and in-person settings  • A proactive mindset and willingness to learn in a fast-paced environment    Who Should Apply?  CUNY students who are:  • Curious about how healthcare and community services intersect  • Passionate about equity and social impact  • Interested in gaining real-world experience in large-scale public health initiatives  • Excited to contribute meaningfully to work that affects millions of New Yorkers    Work Schedule:  Monday - Friday 9am-5pm    Location:  40 Worth St, 4th Fl, New York, NY 10013

column6: WHO WE ARE:   For nearly 40 years, Riverstone Senior Life Services has been dedicated to providing services that enable older adults to remain safely in their homes and communities, enjoying the highest quality of life for as long as they choose. Our commitment to creating bright alternatives for older adults and individuals with memory loss and their caregivers is embodied in our Older Adult Center and Memory Center (social adult day program). Additionally, our Social Service Department focuses on supporting frail and isolated older adults, addressing various psychosocial needs such as benefits connection, eviction prevention, and money management. All of our programs are offered in both Spanish and English, reflecting our dedication to inclusivity and cultural sensitivity. You will have the opportunity to work closely with our dynamic team and contribute to developing strategies that resonate with our target audience. This internship offers hands-on experience in a nonprofit setting and the chance to make a meaningful impact in the lives of older adults, individuals with memory loss, and their caregivers.     • Assist in the development and execution of marketing campaigns to promote Riverstone's programs and services.  • Create engaging content for digital platforms, including social media, newsletters, and the organization's website.  • Collaborate with the Development Manager to develop visually appealing materials, such as brochures, flyers, and promotional materials.  • Support the coordination of events, community outreach, and engagement initiatives.     INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:   • Strategic Marketing Skills: Gain hands-on experience creating and implementing marketing strategies to promote nonprofit services.  • Content Creation: Hone your writing and design skills by developing engaging content for diverse communication channels.  • Community Outreach: Learn the importance of community engagement and how to connect with diverse audiences effectively.  • Nonprofit Operations: Gain insights into the operations of a nonprofit organization.  • Cultural Sensitivity: Develop an understanding of the importance of providing services in both Spanish and English, which fosters inclusivity and cultural sensitivity     TYPE OF SUPERVISION:  Riverstone will provide structured and supportive supervision to interns as they will be part of the Outreach and Engagement team. Interns will receive guidance from their direct supervisor (Development Manager), who oversees the team’s projects and professional development.    Supervision will include weekly team meetings, typically held at the beginning of the week, where staff and interns review projects currently in progress, discuss upcoming initiatives, and reflect on completed work. These meetings create an opportunity for interns to receive constructive feedback from both peers and the supervisor, ask questions, and learn collaborative problem-solving approaches. column6: PLEASE INSERT ALL THE REQUESTED INFORMATION BELOW:    WHO WE ARE:    The Arthur Ashe Institute for Urban Health (AAIUH), founded by the late tennis champion and humanitarian, Arthur Ashe, is a community-based organization that utilizes a model of Community Health Empowerment to address health inequities in multi-ethnic underserved communities. AAIUH works to research and develop innovative community health empowerment programs, provide evidence-based behavioral health interventions in community settings that help participants address chronic health conditions and advocate for their health, prepare underrepresented minority urban youth to succeed in college and become healthcare providers, and improve healthcare providers’ capacity to address racial health disparities through conferences, trainings, and workshops. By working on current relevant public health issues under the supervision and mentorship of experienced professionals, students will take theoretical concepts learned in the classroom and apply them to improve the health and well-being of the community. Participating interns will have exposure to community settings, like barbershops and salons, support program/intervention design and implementation, participate in community engagement and research activities and collaborate with a broad range of stakeholders.   Over the course of the internship period, interns will be expected to support the work of the Institute's Mental Health Peer Leadership program and develop a proposal that will serve as their independent project to supplement and enhance their experience. Projects will be grounded in core public health principles and address existing gaps that will strengthen the Institute’s ability to serve its community. Topic areas will be discussed and developed in partnership with the intern’s mentor/supervisor and will culminate in a presentation at the end of the internship period. column5: Communications Intern -  News Ambassadors (Bridge Alliance Education Fund)
column6: WHO WE ARE:  News Ambassadors (a is a collaborative journalism project housed within Bridge Alliance Education Fund. It enlists college journalism students to help local newsrooms fill gaps in coverage of underreported communities. We uplift solutions and common ground, pairing student journalism classes with local newsrooms, and training them on specific tools including Solutions Journalism and/or depolarization reporting strategies. The depolarization strategies were born from researching conflict mediation psychology studies -- how people actually behave when they're feeling suspicious and threatened by the other side - and distilling lessons journalists can use to improve coverage of contentious issues. Then, they report stories informed by these strategies and by input from community members themselves - so stories will be responsive to local needs and information gaps instead of journalists' assumptions about what news people need. The top stories are shared with local newsroom partners for vetting and possible broadcast. column5: Meeting community information needs Intern - News Ambassadors
column6: WHO WE ARE:  News Ambassadors is a collaborative journalism project housed within Bridge Alliance Education Fund. We enlist college journalism students to help local newsrooms fill gaps in coverage of underreported communities. We uplift solutions and common ground, pairing student journalism classes with local newsrooms, and training them on specific tools including Solutions Journalism and/or depolarization reporting strategies. The depolarization strategies were born from researching conflict mediation psychology studies -- how people actually behave when they're feeling suspicious and threatened by the other side - and distilling lessons journalists can use to improve coverage of contentious issues. Then, they report stories informed by these strategies and by input from community members themselves - so stories will be responsive to local needs and information gaps instead of journalists' assumptions about what news people need. The top stories are shared with local newsroom partners for vetting and possible broadcast. [www.newsambassadors.org and newsambassadors.beehiiv.com ]    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  Writing or reporting journalism articles (in audio or print) would be a welcome job duty for this internship! (Our newsletter focuses on amplifying student journalism work from our program, spotlighting training resources and alumni successes, and highlighting the work we do training student journalists and helping to get their work published by news outlets.)  • Helping to create work flow organization and scheduling for regular trainings, and recruiting additional potential partners.  • Collaborating work /proofreading for clarity and messaging  • Other duties as opportunity /interest arises    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  • Journalism strategies to help strengthen local communities/support healthy communities (Solutions Journalism, Depolarization Reporting Strategies and Community Engagement journalism)  • Collaboration/coordination/ strategizing for current and upcoming newsletter editions (Asana, Airtable, Slack)    REQUIREMENTS/QUALIFICATIONS:  Clear communication/ writing skills  Organizational skills/follow-through  Ability to ask questions when further explanation is needed  Responsibility/accountability for follow through on assignments and initiative to request help or further explanation when necessary - ("NO question is stupid" motto - Please feel comfortable asking column5: Software Intern - AuriStor
column6: What we are  AuriStor is a NY-based company that develops software defined storage technology products used by major financial institutions, departments of defense/energy/interior, and major research universities.    What we make    AuriStor provides AuriStorFS, a cloud native secure distributed file system that allows organizations store their data in any combination of hybrid/multi clouds and access it directly from any device, server or Kubernetes pods.  Our newest techology offering, the AuriStor Container Accelerator allows enterprise applications to be distributed and start up to 95% faster.    Why this is important  Whether you are doing AI/Machine Learning, or just managing project files, storage is a core component. People often are under the impression that "Storage is a solved problem", however they will learn that this is not the case when they need to develop real systems that:       Access huge amounts of data (10s of Terabytes to Petabytes)       Applications that have huge numbers of files (such as with genomic data)       Internal Security and Access Controls are paramount (Medical data, Corporate data, etc)       Secure Data that neeeds to be stored internally to the organization, but accessed externally (open web       Data that must be located both inside your organization and/or one or more different cloud provider       Accessing data from Docker containers       Managing data access across Kubernetes Clusters  Who uses AuriStor products       Major Financial Institutions       US Department of Defense       US Department of Energy       Tier-1 Research Universities  Ongoing AuriStor Projects           AuriStorFS - The AuriStor Global Namespace Secure File System               AuriStorFS Customer Facing Dashboard - A web-based dashboard that allows customers to manage their AuriStorFS instances, monitor performance, and configure settings.               AuriStorFS Cloud Deployment - Tooling to deploy AuriStorFS instances into AWS, Azure, and GCP               AuriStorFS AI Assistant - An AI-powered tool to assist with managing and optimizing AuriStorFS instances.               AuriStorFS Agent - Agentic interaction with AuriStorFS Cluster                         AuriStor Container Accelerator (ACA) - addresses the "Software and container deployment" issues for organizations that are deploying applications across thousands to 100's of thousands of machines/devices              You can learn about ACA by watching this presentation:  https://www.auristor.com/video/ACA-20231004.mp4               ACA Customer Facing Dashboard - A web-based dashboard that allows customers to manage their ACA instances, monitor performance, and configure settings.               ACA Cloud Deployment - Tooling to deploy ACA instances into AWS, Azure, and GCP               ACA AI Assistant - An AI-powered tool to assist with managing and optimizing ACA instances.               ACA Agent - Agentic interaction with ACA  NOTE: This IS NOT a novice internship.   Internships at AuriStor are only appropriate for students with a strong background in computer science, software engineering, or related fields.         Internship projects will be assigned by AuriStor based on the student's skills and background.     You will not choose your own project, but you will be able to express your preferences. As part of your application process you will be required to provide:       Which project(s) you are interested in       Justification for why you are best suited to work on that project       Detailed information about technical background, prior experience, and GitHub link  Who will you work under:  You will directly report to Gerry Seidman who has had dozens of interns who have gone on to work at companies  including Google, Amazon, EA, and various major financial institutions.  His goal is that, more than just honing technical skills, you get skills to help you become an architect of next generations of high performance distributed systems.    Internship is fully remote and schedule will be discussed AFTER the interns are selected/accepted

column5: Harlem Community Planning and Marketing Intern -  Harlem One Stop Inc
column6: Who We Are  Harlem One Stop is a nonprofit that works to celebrate and strengthen Harlem through neighborhood tours, arts and culture marketing, public events, destination branding, and commercial revitalization. Based in Hamilton Heights, our small and experienced team works at the intersection of culture, community development, and local engagement.    We are launching a public space study to better understand Harlem’s parks, plazas, and other shared spaces—and to explore how they can be more welcoming, accessible, and useful for the people who live, study, and spend time here.    This is a hands-on internship. You will spend time out in the community, learning how to collect information, talk with residents, observe how public spaces are used, and help turn that information into ideas and communications that support neighborhood improvement.    Duties & Responsibilities  * Pedestrian Counts: Count foot traffic at about 9 locations using a clicker or pen and paper, with repeat visits at different times of day. This helps us understand how spaces are used and where outreach and investment may be needed. (~4 hrs/week)  * Photography: Take photos and short videos to document how public spaces are used and identify things that could be improved. This may include showing positive activity, documenting conditions, and supporting your observations.  * Resident Interviews: Conduct short surveys using a prepared script and provided tools, in print or online, in English and Spanish. Training and support will be provided. All responses are anonymous. (~4 hrs/week)  * Observation: Record how people use public spaces—such as sitting, socializing, exercising, or relaxing—using a structured observation tool at different locations and times. (~6 hrs/week)  * Communications Research & Development: Review current outreach and promotion related to public space, and use your field research findings from pedestrian counts, observations, interviews, and documentation to help improve communication tools. This may include helping identify neighborhood information, messages, or formats that build awareness, encourage participation, and support stewardship of shared spaces. (~5 hrs/week)  * Connecting the Research: All parts of this project work together. You will help turn what you see, hear, and measure into clear findings, useful ideas, and stronger communications. For example, if foot traffic is high in one area but interviews and observations show concerns about seating or safety, you may help identify practical ideas for improvement.  * Additional Support: You may also help with local business promotion, community events, and other project tasks based on organizational needs and your interests.    This is a strong resume-building internship where your work will contribute to real planning, outreach, and neighborhood improvement efforts in Harlem.    By the End of the Internship, You’ll Build Skills In:  * Community outreach: Talk with residents and gather helpful feedback.  * Research and data collection: Conduct surveys, observations, interviews, and pedestrian counts.  * Communications and outreach materials: Use research findings to help improve messages and outreach tools.  * Data analysis: Organize information and turn it into clear findings and ideas.  * Public space and neighborhood research: Learn how parks, plazas, and other shared spaces are studied and improved.  * Teamwork and professional communication: Build confidence sharing updates, asking questions, and working with staff.  * Events and local promotion: Support community events and help promote neighborhood spaces and local businesses.    You will also have the chance to shape your experience based on your interests, whether that is research, writing, marketing, policy, or community engagement. column6: WHO WE ARE:  My Caring Wish strengthens community self-reliance by connecting people, skills, and resources through education and empowerment. We exist to create safe, empowering spaces where youth and families build emotional resilience, financial confidence, and lifelong wellness skills. We conduct engaging workshops, year-round programming, and guest speaking sessions in communities and at schools for students, adults, and staff, delivering practical tools in mental wellness and financial literacy in ways that are interactive, relatable, and transformative.     DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  Position Overview  This internship offers a high-impact opportunity for a motivated college student interested in nonprofit leadership, business development, and strategic partnerships. The intern will work directly with organizational leadership to expand national visibility, secure funding, and position the organization for speaking engagements and institutional partnerships. This role develops real-world skills in grant development, professional outreach, marketing strategy, and executive-level communications.     Key Responsibilities  ·         Grant Development: Research and support the submission of 2 targeted grant applications per week, building a structured pipeline of funding opportunities aligned with organizational initiatives.  ·         Speaking Engagement Outreach: Identify and secure speaking engagements at universities and educational institutions nationwide through strategic outreach to departments, program directors, and event coordinators.  ·         University Partnership Research: Build and maintain a targeted database of universities and departments (e.g., education, business, psychology, wellness, student affairs) aligned with the organization’s programming.  ·         Conference Speaker Placement: Research domestic and international conferences seeking speakers and submit proposals to position the organization as a featured presenter.  ·         Presentation & Marketing Support: Assist in developing professional presentation decks and outreach materials that effectively communicate program impact to institutions and event organizers.  ·         Brand Visibility Strategy: Identify cost-effective branded marketing materials and promotional swag that enhance brand recognition and support contract acquisition at events. column5: Constituent Services and legislative Affairs Intern - Office of Council Member Hudson
column6: Crystal is the Council Member for New York City’s District 35 in Brooklyn, representing the neighborhoods of Crown Heights, Prospect Heights, Clinton Hill, and Fort Greene. A third-generation Brooklynite, she was first elected in 2021 and made history as one of the first out gay Black women ever elected in New York City. Crystal is a public servant committed to making government more accessible for more people. As a first-term Council Member, she passed more bills than any other first-term member in Brooklyn and was second among all new members. She has authored the Black Agenda for New York City and co-authored the Marsha & Sylvia Plan, a first-of-its-kind policy agenda to support LGBTQIA+ New Yorkers. Crystal is chair of the Committee on Aging and also serves as co-chair of the Council’s Black, Latino, and Asian Caucus.    About the Role  The Intern will be a vital part of the entire office’s operations - from scheduling and communications to legislation, constituent services, and budget. This vital role provides The Intern with a comprehensive understanding of all aspects of local government and the role the City Council plays in the lives of the more than 8.8 million New Yorkers. We are seeking someone who is interested in learning about all facets of local government, able to communicate well with people from all backgrounds, and eager to help make local government more accessible to more people.    Responsibilities  The Intern is integral to supporting all positions within the office, including the Council Member and Chief of Staff. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:  Providing resources and services to the general public via constituent service requests;  Cultivating and maintaining relationships with direct service providers, advocacy organizations, city and state agencies, and any other offices that could aid in constituent services;  Applying an inclusive, anti-racist approach to service delivery;  Developing policy and budget priorities derived from the Council Member’s policy positions, constituent and community issues, data and other sources;  Keeping track of legislative, constituent services, and budgetary data via spreadsheets and software;  Drafting written content for the Council Member, including social media posts and talking points;  Identifying digital & social media trends, and making recommendations for how the office can leverage those trends to expand its reach;  Assisting in maintaining and overseeing the schedule of the Council Member;  Cultivating and maintaining relationships with community stakeholders, elected officials and their staff, city agencies, advocacy groups, and Council staff;  Staffing the Council Member and representing the office at public events;  Helping to maintain effective internal and external communications;  Fielding constituent inquiries and requests; and  Other duties as assigned.    Qualifications  The Intern role is for someone who is passionate about public service, eager to learn the ins-and-outs of government, and willing to take on any task, big or small. Qualifications should include, but are not limited to:    Experience or interest in public service and making a difference through local government;  Some familiarity with or interest in city agencies and government offices;  Excellent written, digital, and oral communication skills;  Collaborative approach centered in equity;  Keen attention to detail and superb organization skills;  Ability to build and nurture relationships both within and outside of government;  Comfortable communicating with people from all backgrounds;  Strong ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment; and  Ability to think and act fast in moments of crisis with calm focus.    Who You Are  You are friendly, complete tasks thoroughly and efficiently, and always eager to learn new things.  You are excited to make a difference through local government, and will do so with a sense of  humor and an egoless approach to your work. You’re also someone who works hard and is  dependable. column6: WHO WE ARE:  Art Beyond Sight (ABS) supports disabled people to be active, creative, and powerful participants and contributors in the arts and, through the arts, in society- at large. ABS inspires and provides resources across the cultural sector for the full integration of disabled people in arts and cultural institutions. You can learn more about us below.    The New York City Mental Health Collective, working in collaboration with Art Beyond Sight, is a grassroots coalition of more than 35 organizations dedicated to promoting health equity and advancing the rights and inclusion of people with mental health conditions and other disabilities through the power of creative storytelling to evoke emotions and connection with others. You can learn more about Art Beyond Sight and the New York City Mental Health Collective below.    ABOUT THE PROJECT:  Name: NYCMHC Voices Unbound: A Storytelling Initiative for Disability, Mental Health, and Community Empowerment  The project provides a space for individuals with lived experience  in mental health and other disabilities to share their personal stories to evoke emotions and connection with others through digital media. Amplifying  will shift public understanding, reduce stigma, and build community-driven solutions that focus on the needs and wisdom of those most affected.    Project Goals  1. Elevating first-person stories from communities whose voices are rarely heard.  2. Increasing  public awareness of systemic barriers within disability, mental health communities, and other marginalized communities.  3. Using storytelling as a tool for healing, empowerment, and advocacy.  4. Promoting inclusive, human-centered policy and practice by sharing stories with service providers, advocates, and decision-makers.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  With direction and supervision, participants will assist with creating ideas for creative storytelling and developing interview questions based on the target audience. In addition, participants will attend citywide public events and workshops to digitally interview New Yorkers as well as assist with editing CapCut for social media content. They will:  - Serve as the face of ABS at public events and the Disability Unite Festival, assisting attendees and providing information about activities, directions, and access accommodations.  - Create a welcoming, inclusive environment for all participants.  - Conduct follow-up surveys and contribute to reporting to inform improvements for future events and accessibility programming.  - Support the media and communications team, including documenting events and promoting content online.  - Develop storytelling-focused interview questions tailored to specific target audiences.  - Conduct interviews to capture compelling personal stories and insights.  - Edit and produce creative story content using CapCut.    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  - Strong communication and customer service skills with diverse populations.  - Knowledge of accessibility needs, disability accommodations, and practical inclusion strategies.  - Multitasking, attention to detail, and ability to collaborate with others in fast-paced environments.  - Professional growth through hands-on experience in community organizing and accessibility coordination.  - Flexibility and adaptability to changing situations and needs  - Confidence in digitally conveying others experiencing through storytelling  - Gain confidence, build key skills, and get real-world experience. By the end of your internship, your resume will reflect your growth.    REQUIREMENTS:   - Excellent communication skills and ability to engage a wide audience.  - Empathy and sensitivity to diverse needs, with attention to cultural, linguistic, and intersectional accessibility considerations.  - Strong organizational and multitasking abilities.  - Familiarity with social media, digital tools, and accessible communications.  - Ability to work under pressure and adapt to changing situations.  - Customer service skills, including the ability to provide a positive and welcoming experience for attendees    WORK SCHEDULE:  We offer a flexible schedule, but request students have a “base-level” overlap with their fellow interns anytime during the 9 - 5 workday on either Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday. These do not have to be consecutive hours.    Please try to keep these dates open – (not mandatory, but appreciated):  • Sunday, July 12th - Disability Unite Festival, Naumburg Bandshell in Central Park  • Sunday, July 26 - Anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act  • July Disability Pride Month activities in each Borough with the City Council and the NYC Mayor’s Office. These dates are not scheduled yet.  • Other events- Community events, workshops, conferences, and parades. Dates have not been scheduled as yet.    LOCATION:  Hybrid - We believe in remote work as an access accommodation. You may work remotely in our 24/7 "Zoom office", or hybrid with in-person work at our partner sites throughout NYC. Our office Location is in SoHo 589 Broadway New York, NY 10012 (cross street is Houston Street) in Manhattan.    You will also attend the in-person events outlined in the work schedule above.    ABOUT US:  This internship is led by Art Beyond Sight through Project Access for All, in active partnership with Disability Pride NYC, Disability Unite,  and the NYC Mental Health Collective and a broad consortium of disability, cultural, athletic, civic, and public-sector partners citywide. Originally developed through federal and New York City disability workgroups, Project Access for All established a lasting framework for local and national collaboration. The internship is supervised by Art Beyond Sight staff, with regular mentorship meetings from leaders across this consortium, providing hands-on experience and strategic insight into how large-scale accessibility initiatives are built, implemented, and sustained.    Art Beyond Sight leads Project Access for All, the first and only open-source national platform advancing accessibility, inclusion, and systemic change across arts, culture, recreation, and civic life. Through Project Access NYC and the launch of NYC Belongs, we are building district-level partnerships across all 51 City Council districts to strengthen community accessibility infrastructure.    We work at the intersection of disability leadership, cultural institutions, parks and athletics, technology, youth engagement, and public policy — ensuring that access is not an afterthought, but part of how New York City leads. We partner with Disability Pride NYC and Disability Unite—including the annual Disability Unite Festival—and collaborate closely with Independent Living Centers, disability advocacy organizations, arts and cultural institutions, parks and athletic organizations, and entertainment venues across the city.    NYC Belongs is powered by emerging leaders ready to build real change. Through this summer initiative, students gain direct, hands-on engagement with the diverse stakeholders that shape our communities — from grassroots disability advocates to major civic and cultural institutions — building practical skills, professional confidence, and meaningful relationships while advancing systemic change.    NYC Belongs is a fast-moving, multi-team initiative with many moving parts. We are building something ambitious — and we are committed to doing it in a way that is organized, sustainable, and human-centered.    ABOUT THE FOUNDER OF THE NYC MENTAL HEALTH COLLECTIVE:  Christina Sparrock is a Certified Public Accountant and mental health advocate who draws on her lived experience with a mental health condition to advance disability, racial, and social justice. She spent nearly two decades as a Crisis Response Expert and was among the early members of Correct Crisis Intervention Today–NYC. As a Certified Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) Trainer, she has trained law enforcement agencies including the NYPD, the Department of Corrections, and the NYC Parks Department on de-escalation and respectful engagement with individuals experiencing emotional crisis.    In 2020, Sparrock created the Person-Centered Intervention Training (PCIT) Mental Health Response Program in Fort Greene Park, the first park-based mental health response program of its kind. PCIT-trained Peer Specialists—known as the Social Well-Being Team—support park visitors experiencing challenges such as mental health or substance use issues, homelessness, or involvement with the criminal justice system. The program’s success has led to expansion across additional parks in New York City.    Sparrock is the founding member of the NYC Mental Health Collective, which promotes dialogue and advocacy for equitable mental health services. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the Collective hosted the first virtual NYC Mental Health Mayoral Candidate Town Hall, featuring nine mayoral candidates and attracting over 2,700 viewers.  She currently serves on several mental health and public health initiatives, including the Daniel’s Law Task Force appointed by the New York State Office of Mental Health, Brooklyn Borough President Antonio Reynoso’s Maternal Health Task Force, and the NYC Department of Health Maternal Mortality Review Committee. Sparrock is also a board member of the Center for Independence of the Disabled, New York (CIDNY). She is currently pursuing a Master of Arts in Urban Studies with a focus on healthcare policy.

WHO WE ARE:  ADAPT Community Network is the leading human service not-for-profit and a pioneer in providing innovative programs and services for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.    SUMMARY:   In this internship, you'll be helping to build a more inclusive world by stepping into the heart of person-centered support at Manhattan Day Hab 2 & 6 at 5030 Broadway, New York, NY 10034 .     This role offer a front-row seat to the 'human' side of NON-CLINICAL care, perfect for students curious about Psychology/Behavioral Science, Social Work/Human Services, Sociology, Disabilities Studies, Nonprofit Management, Nursing/Healthcare Service, Music/Art/Drama Therapy, Public Health and Policy, and more.     You’ll empower adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities to grow daily living skills, make choices, and connect with their community through person-centered plans, structured activities, and social engagement on-site and out in the community.     WORK SCHEDULE:  This is an entirely in-person position. Adult Day Habilitation program hours are typically Monday - Friday, 8:00 AM – 3:00 PM. You will work with you intern manager/program director to create a schedule that is mutually beneficial and allows both the you and program to achieve goals.    Note: Interns may not touch, transport, or dispense any medication (including over-the-counter medicines). Interns also do not provide direct toileting, feeding, or dressing.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  This internship may include a mixture of hands-on and administrative work.    Person-Centered Support  • Partner with professional staff to implement individualized plans reflecting each supported person’s strengths, preferences, and goals.  • Offer respectful prompts and assistance that encourage choice-making, self-advocacy, and independence.  • Ensure safety and well-being through attentive supervision and protective oversight.    Skill-Building & Community Inclusion  • Help facilitate structured activities, e.g., classes in gaming, cooking, crafting, computer, music, mindfulness, and more.  • Support practice of social-skills in conversation, self-advocacy, problem-solving, and relationship-building.  • Assist with safe, purposeful outings (e.g., libraries, parks, visiting friends, local businesses) to build and strengthen real-world skills.    Program Implementation  • Set up, facilitate, and wrap up activities; maintain a clean, organized program space.  • Assist staff in following behavior or treatment plans.  • Track participation and progress; assist with simple documentation (case notes, incident reporting, etc.).    Teamwork & Program Support  • Work closely with fellow interns and all staff including Program Directors and their teams.  • Contribute to an uplifting, positive, and proactive team environment while completing work in a manner free from recognized hazards.  • Participate in in-service training and learning opportunities provided by ADAPT.    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  • Professional Experience in disability services, direct care, and person-centered support.  • Teamwork & Collaboration by working as part of an interdisciplinary support team.  • Program Implementation by learning how to facilitate life-skills, vocational, and social-skills activities that build real independence.  • Community Integration by learning best practices for planning purposeful outings and reinforcing travel and community-use skills.  • Leadership & Responsibility by modeling positive behavior, initiative, and accountability.  • Cultural Competency by supporting diverse individuals and embracing diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility, and belonging.    QUALIFICATIONS  These qualifications will help make your internship more engaging and rewarding:  • Strong oral and written communication skills with the ability to read, write, and communicate clearly in English.  • Ability to sit, stand, and move throughout the day in a dynamic, multi-sensory environment (e.g., music, conversation, activity sounds, etc.)  • Positive people skills for collaborating with coworkers, supervisors, people we support, and their families.  • Willingness to listen, learn, and ask questions when unsure.  • Ability to recognize and help solve problems, including seeking guidance from trained staff when needed.  • Patience, flexibility, and a supportive attitude in resolving conflicts or managing stressful situations.  • Openness to learning about disability services and DEIAB (diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility, and belonging).  • A collaborative spirit and respect for diverse perspectives.    SUPERVISION  Interns are supervised by Program Directors and/or designated professional staff at their work locations.    NOTE:  ADAPT Community Network can make reasonable accommodations to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.    Because ADAPT Community Network serves a vulnerable population, we require all interns to successfully complete a pre-employment screening process. This includes a criminal background check, fingerprinting, and a negative tuberculosis test. column5: Marketing & Communications Intern – Scandinavian Market LLC
column6: WHO WE ARE:  Björk Café & Bistro is a Scandinavian café and catering company located inside Scandinavia House in Midtown Manhattan. Our mission is to share Nordic food, hospitality, and culture through a welcoming café experience and thoughtfully curated catering and events. We specialize in Nordic-inspired cuisine, pastries, and beverages while also providing catering for corporate events, receptions, and private gatherings. Our team values creativity, collaboration, and creating memorable guest experiences through food and service.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  Assist with social media planning, content creation, and posting (primarily Instagram)  Support marketing initiatives for the café, including seasonal menus, promotions, and events  Assist with promoting catering services and private events  Draft marketing and communication materials such as newsletters, event announcements, and promotional text  Help update and organize website content and digital marketing materials  Assist with photography or visual content creation for marketing and social media  Research potential partnerships, community outreach opportunities, and event collaborations  Help organize marketing assets, communication materials, and promotional content  Provide light support for event promotion and marketing for café programming    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  Social media marketing and content planning  Digital marketing strategies for restaurants and hospitality businesses  Marketing communications and promotional writing  Brand development and storytelling for a small business  Event marketing and promotion  Basic marketing analytics and performance tracking  Professional communication and collaboration in a hospitality environment  Project organization and marketing campaign coordination    REQUIREMENTS?QUALIFICATIONS:  Interns must sign a confidentiality agreement on their first day, agreeing not to share any company passwords, user IDs, or other confidential information during or after the internship  Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Marketing, Communications, Hospitality, or a related field  Strong interest in social media, digital marketing, and the hospitality industry  Experience or familiarity with Instagram content creation and visual storytelling  Excellent written and verbal communication skills; strong proficiency in English required  Creative, organized, and self-motivated with the ability to manage multiple projects  Basic skills in photography, video, or design tools (e.g., Canva, Adobe Suite) preferred  Interest in Nordic culture, food, or design is a plus  Comfortable working both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment    SUPERVISION:  The intern will work closely with the café’s management team and will be supervised by the Catering & Events Coordinator. The intern will receive guidance on marketing projects, communications, and campaigns, as well as feedback on written materials and content creation. Weekly check-ins will be held to review progress, discuss new projects, and provide mentorship and support. The intern will also receive training on the café’s brand, marketing goals, and communication strategies.    WORK SCHEDULE:  DAYS/TIME: Monday–Friday between approximately 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM. The intern’s schedule can be flexible within these hours depending on academic commitments. Occasional coordination during café events or promotions will be scheduled in advance.    LOCATION:  In-person  Björk Café & Bistro  Scandinavia House  58 Park Avenue  New York, NY 10016    NOTE:  This is an in-person internship designed to give students hands-on experience in marketing and communications within the hospitality industry. The intern will gain exposure to both café operations and catering/event promotion. Training and onboarding will be provided at the beginning of the internship to familiarize the student with the brand, marketing tools, and current initiatives.

column5: Chapter Establishment & Development Fellow – FLIP National
column6: WHO WE ARE:  ""FLIP" is an acronym; it stands for First-Generation Low-Income Partnership.  FLIP National is a national non-profit organization that does advocacy work on behalf of first-generation and/or low-income (FGLI) college students at colleges & universities across the country.  Our organizational structure is similar to that of fraternities & sororities; that is, there is a national organization with chapters at different schools around the country.  We currently have 32 chapters and counting, and we have actively built a number of tools & resources that can benefit any efforts to affect positive change on a college campus for FGLI students.   Our core tenet is that we center student advocacy & the student voice, which is why our chapters are dedicated, student-run FGLI student organizations.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  - Working with schools to start student organizations  - Helping existing student organizations address FGLI student issues on campus  - Spearheading efforts to implement national initiatives (i.e., FLIP National initiatives) at the campus level  - Engaging in the substantive crafting of policy & initiatives that will make life better for FGLI students on college campuses across the country    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  - Negotiation  - Project management  - Design thinking  - Program design  - Event planning    SUPERVISION  All FLIP National fellows are required to attend 1 weekly check-in every week.  There are multiple opportunities to attend a weekly check-in, but each fellow only needs to attend one check-in per week.  This is in addition to any team meetings that may get scheduled.  Due to the nature of the workflow in this role (meetings with prospective & current chapters), there is more of a time commitment for chapter establishment & development fellows than there is for other teams.  The Chapter Establishment & Development team will also have a weekly training to help new fellows learn the concepts they will need to understand to be able to do the work of the team.  Chapter Establishment & Development fellows also attend meeting with both prospective and current chapters.  Before each meeting with a prospective or current chapter, we meet for half an hour for a prep session to go over everything folks need to know going into the meeting, and to ensure we are all on the same page regarding what the purpose of the meeting is and what needs to be covered/addressed during the meeting.  These meetings are scheduled based on the availability of the prospective or current chapters; chapter establishment & development fellows are expected to attend any and all meetings they are available to be present for.    WORK SCHEDULE:  Weekly check-in time slots are TBD before the fellowship begins for the summer and is based on the stated availability of fellows selected for the fellowship.  Evenings, late nights and weekends are all possibilities for meeting times both for internal mandatory meetings and for meetings with prospective or current chapters.  The nature of the workflow of the fellowship is much more task-oriented than it is time-oriented.  When a fellow is given a task, it is of less concern how much time the fellow takes to complete the task and of more concern that the task actually gets completed.    LOCATION:  Virtual    NOTE:  - As part of the application process, we have a proprietary form that you will need to fill out to be considered for the fellowship.  Please fill out the application form BEFORE submitting your application on this platform.  - If you are assigned to a team as part of being selected for the fellowship, that does not preclude you from working on projects that fall under the purview of other teams in the fellowship.  The FLIP National Fellowship is a learning environment, and we foster an environment where fellows have the ability to learn any and all skills they're interested in learning about.  - NO EXPERIENCE IS REQUIRED FOR ANY ROLE IN THE FLIP NATIONAL FELLOWSHIP.  We will provide training, guidance and resources to help fellows perform any tasks for any roles in the fellowship.  - Due to the nature of the workflow in this role (meetings with prospective & current chapters), there is more of a time commitment for chapter establishment & development fellows than there is for other teams.  - Meetings with prospective and current chapters are scheduled based on the availability of the prospective or current chapter, so the frequency of meetings is difficult to anticipate.  Chapter establishment & development fellows should be prepared to be flexible in terms of their availability for meetings.

column5: AI Course Development Internship
column6: WHO WE ARE  PYE Education Center (Perfect Your Education) is an innovative, tech-forward education center dedicated to helping students master math, ELA, History, Science, and tech skills through engaging in-person classes and educational platforms with interactive courses. We integrate cutting-edge AI tools to create dynamic learning experiences and give college students and recent grads hands-on opportunities to build the future of education.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES  Design and build AI-powered online courses from concept to completion. Interns will participate in a structured course creation process centered around building a full 50-lesson course from the ground up.    Each course is broken into 50 clearly defined lessons, and each lesson follows a consistent, professional structure:    Step 1: Topic Breakdown and Planning  Interns begin by identifying and organizing the 50 lesson topics within a subject. This includes outlining the progression of difficulty, ensuring logical flow, and defining clear learning objectives for each lesson.    Step 2: Introduction Page Creation  Each lesson begins with an introduction page that explains what the student will learn. This page includes:    A clear lesson objective  Key vocabulary or concepts  A brief real-world connection or application  A preview of what will be covered    Step 3: AI Video Walkthrough Lesson  Interns then create a full learning page centered around a video walkthrough. This is one of the most important components of the course. Using AI tools, interns:    Write a structured script that teaches the concept step-by-step  Break content into slides or segments (each slide designed for 7 to 10 seconds of reading time)  Use AI tools (such as Multi-platform Game Dev., Agentic AIs, or similar platforms) to generate visuals, explanations, and interactive elements  Ensure the explanation is clear, engaging, and appropriate for the target student level    Step 4: Quiz Creation (5 to 10 Questions)  After the lesson, interns create a quiz to assess understanding. Each quiz includes:    5 to 10 multiple-choice questions  Balanced answer choices (A, B, C, D evenly distributed)  Questions directly aligned with the lesson content  An answer key with clear explanations for each question    Step 5: Short Answer Response  Each lesson concludes with a short-answer question designed to deepen understanding. This encourages:    Critical thinking  Personal reflection on the concept  Application of the lesson in a new context    Step 6: AI Enhancement and Interactivity  Throughout the lesson creation process, interns integrate AI-driven elements such as:    Mind maps for concept visualization  Flowcharts for processes  Slides and whiteboard-style explanations  Interactive prompts and guided learning scenarios    Step 7: Review and Iteration  Interns collaborate with team members to review and refine lessons. This includes:    Peer editing and feedback  Revising scripts and questions  Improving clarity, engagement, and instructional quality    In addition to course creation, interns will:  Draft lesson texts and create engaging scripts for instructional videos  Develop multiple-choice and open-ended quiz questions with answer keys and explanations  Incorporate interactive elements (mind maps, flowcharts, slides, whiteboards, etc.) using AI tools like Multi-platform Game Dev., Agentic AIs or similar  Collaborate with our education and technical teams to ensure quality and consistency across modules  Research emerging AI tools and propose innovative features for course delivery    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP    AI-assisted course design and instructional design best practices  Educational content writing and assessment creation  Project management and collaborative workflow in an agile, creative environment  Practical skills in integrating AI technologies (e.g., Multi-platform Game Dev., Agentic AIs) into e-learning  Digital publishing and LMS (Moodle) setup    SUPERVISION  Interns receive direct mentorship from Steve Salowsky, PYE founder and Headmaster, along with weekly guidance from our senior instructional designers. Regular check-ins, content reviews, and brainstorming sessions provide professional support and feedback throughout the internship.    WORK SCHEDULE  Days/Time: Flexible scheduling of about 19 hours per week, with optional daily team meetings, and asynchronous work    Start/End Date: early July and mid-August    LOCATION: Fully remote, HQ out of our offices in Queens

column6: WHO WE ARE  Well Read Sistas Inc. is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to the personal, professional, and cultural development of Black women through literature, intentional community, and cultural programming.  We create spaces where Black women gather to read, reflect, build, and grow together through book discussions, wellness initiatives, and leadership experiences rooted in sisterhood.    What Is the Well Read Scholars Program?  The Well Read Scholars Program is our leadership and internship incubator for emerging leaders who want hands-on experience inside a growing nonprofit organization.  This is a build-it-with-us experience where Scholars actively contribute to the programming, infrastructure, and community engagement that powers Well Read Sistas Inc. Scholars gain real tools to move confidently through professional and personal spaces while being grounded in self-knowledge, collective care, and Black brilliance.    Summer 2026 Required Reading  All Scholars must read and review:  The Student's Guide to Financial Freedom  One additional book voted on collectively by Scholars during the first week of the program.  These readings will inform discussions during Book Clubs, Author Chats, Scholar-led Book Club sessions, and Silent Read reflections.    What Scholars Will Experience This Summer  In addition to daily project work, Scholars will participate in:  Speed-Friending: Staff + Scholars Edition  Headshot Clinic & Résumé Development Day  Monthly Book Clubs (July & August)  Author Chats  Scholar-Led Book Club  Interim “Sis, You Good?” Leadership  Signature Etiquette & Professionalism Lessons  Scholars Networking Event  Silent Read Programming  Personalized Letter of Recommendation  What Makes the Well Read Scholars Program Unique  Most internships end when the summer ends.  The Well Read Scholars Program does not. Scholars leave this experience with:  A lifelong network of support from Well Read Sistas mentors and community members  Continued invitations to programming, book clubs, and events  Direct access to Ari, Lavie, and Well Read Sistas leadership for guidance, references, and mentorship  Ongoing monthly Scholar check-ins after the summer concludes  A community of Sistas who know their name, their goals, and their growth  You are not just completing hours. You are becoming part of the Well Read Sistas ecosystem, and each Scholar receives a personalized letter of recommendation at the end of the program.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  As a Well Read Scholar, you will:  Assist with planning and executing Well Read Sistas events  Research books, authors, and discussion themes  Create social media and newsletter content  Conduct membership outreach and warm calls  Support administrative and operational tasks  Assist with flyer distribution across NYC  Support logistics for signature programs and events including:  Sis, You Good? Weekly Check-In  Movie Nite  The BIG Spades League Tournament  Silent Read with Well Read Sistas  Silent Read Logistics (Scholar Role)    Silent Read is one of our most attended and community-centered programs. Scholars will rotate through the following responsibilities:  Venue setup and breakdown  Check-in table and attendance tracking  Greeting and welcoming attendees  Distributing bookmarks or materials  Timekeeping for reading sessions  Capturing content for social media  Supporting reflection/share-out portions after reading  Assisting with vendor or partner coordination when applicable  Post-event follow-up tasks (photos, recap content, attendance log)  Scholars will learn how to manage a program from pre-event planning ? live execution ? post-event follow-up.    Each Scholar selects one primary project to lead or support. Options include:  Newsletter design & editorial content  Planning Movie Nite  Membership engagement calls  Flyer distribution and community outreach  Event staffing and logistics  Mailing prep  Assisting or leading “Sis, You Good?” check-ins  Social media content calendar  Leading the Scholar Book Club  Supporting Silent Read program management  Bonus hours available through asynchronous assignments. Nonprofit & Business Foundations: Business basics, understanding WRS mission, link day (Instagram, Meetup, Canva, Eventbrite), social media calendar planning, customer service, outreach training, membership re-engagement, administrative paperwork. Career & Professional Development: Headshot Day, résumé guidance, professional communication practice, end-of-summer brunch, and post-summer Scholar check-ins.  These elements are intentionally woven into the program through Silent Read logistics, Scholar-led Book Club, headshot & résumé clinic, Sis, You Good? leadership, and signature etiquette lessons. column5: Bronx Zoo Science Education Assistant
column6: WHO WE ARE:  WCS conserves wildlife and wild places worldwide through science, education, and action. Operating in nearly 60 countries, all the world’s oceans, and five NYC wildlife parks—visited by 4 million people annually—we integrate fieldwork with zoo and aquarium expertise. Our Education Department fosters conservation advocacy by connecting people with nature, enhancing scientific literacy, and promoting stewardship.     DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES  Effective communication of complex STEM concepts is essential in the field of science education. As a Science Education Assistant, you will gain hands-on experience in informal science education through the Wildlife Conservation Society’s (WCS) on-site summer camp programming at the Bronx Zoo.  Under the mentorship of WCS educators, you will develop skills in designing, refining, and delivering engaging STEM-based activities across multiple educational programs, including summer camps, weekend workshops, and field trip experiences. This internship provides a unique opportunity to explore science communication strategies, learn best practices in informal STEM education, and apply pedagogical techniques to make scientific principles accessible and exciting for diverse audiences. Throughout the program, you will build transferable skills such as public speaking, curriculum development, and hands-on facilitation of STEM concepts, while working in a professional science education setting. You will gain experience in interpreting biological, ecological, and conservation topics, designing interactive learning experiences, and inspiring the next generation of scientists through innovative educational programming.     LEARNING OUTCOMES  By the end of this internship, participants will:  • Develop collaboration and teamwork skills, learning to work effectively as part of an education team in a professional setting.  • Gain experience in STEM education techniques, including strategies for teaching scientific concepts to diverse audiences in an informal learning environment.  • Strengthen public engagement and customer service skills, gaining confidence in interacting with the public and facilitating science-based discussions.  • Learn effective science communication techniques, including how to translate complex STEM topics into engaging, age-appropriate learning experiences.  • Build curriculum development skills, gaining experience in designing, adapting, and delivering interactive, hands-on STEM activities.  • Develop an understanding of informal education methodologies, including different teaching styles, inquiry-based learning, and interactive facilitation strategies.  • Gain insight into the operations of a nonprofit cultural organization, with a focus on education, outreach, and mission-driven programming.  • Expand knowledge of environmental and wildlife conservation, including key ecological concepts, conservation challenges, and solutions.  • Learn about WCS’s active conservation initiatives and the diverse range of STEM careers that support wildlife conservation efforts globally.  • Understand the connections between urban environments and nature, and explore the role of conservation-minded actions in daily life.  • Gain professional development experience, building transferable skills such as leadership, adaptability, problem-solving, and effective communication.    SUPERVISION  Interns will be supervised by experienced WCS educators who will provide daily on-site guidance, with regular check-ins to review progress, set goals, and address questions. Students will receive ongoing mentorship through direct feedback and access to training resources that support skill development in science communication, curriculum design, and informal STEM education.    SCHEULE:   Monday-Friday, 3-4 hours a day (9am-5pm depending on the day) and/or 10:30am-5pm on weekends.     LOCATION:  Bronx Zoo- 2300 Southern Boulevard, Bronx, NY 10460    NOTES:   All accepted students must have an interest in working with children in grades K-8 and successfully pass a background screening (provided by WCS).

The ASRC is designed to promote a unique, interdisciplinary research culture with researchers from each of the initiatives working side by side in the ASRC’s core facilities, sharing equipment that is among the most advanced available. column6: WHO WE ARE:  The New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) is the nation’s largest municipal housing preservation and development agency. Its mission is to promote quality housing and diverse, thriving neighborhoods for New Yorkers through loan and development programs for new affordable housing, preservation of the affordability of the existing housing stock, enforcement of housing quality standards, and educational programs for tenants and building owners    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  Your Team:  The Office of Neighborhood Strategies is charged with ensuring that HPD’s development and preservation efforts are guided by meaningful community engagement and coordinated with public investments in infrastructure and services, as put forth in the Mayor's Housing Plan.     The Office of Neighborhood Strategies is composed of two divisions and a special unit reporting to the Associate Commissioner:   -Planning & Predevelopment (P&P) is central to developing and managing HPD's housing production pipeline from project proposal phases through the land use review and entitlement process, to ensure that HPD's investments contribute to building strong, healthy, resilient neighborhoods in all five boroughs.   -Neighborhood?Development & Stabilization (ND&S) leads the agency's commitment to neighborhood planning and strategic preservation through engagement with tenants, landlords, community leaders, and neighborhood stakeholders as we work to enable strong and healthy neighborhoods anchored by affordable housing.   -The Strategic Initiatives Unit is a special team that works across these Divisions to provide essential technical, planning, and policy support to ONS staff and the Deputy Commissioner of Neighborhood Strategies.     Your Impact:   As an Affordable Housing and Community Engagement Intern, for the Office of Neighborhood Strategies' Predevelopment and Urban Design team you will assist with the community visioning phase of the Request for Proposals (RFP) process for publicly owned sites. You will also collaborate with the Communications team to support outreach and messaging efforts. You will explore the ways in which affordable housing projects processes intersect with local communities and develop skills in public outreach, communications, and effective engagement strategies for New Yorkers. This is a hands-on internship well suited to students interested in urban planning, public engagement, public service, or community development.     INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  The Affordable Housing and Community Engagement Intern will be expected to:   - Conduct research on neighborhoods, stakeholders, and affordable housing programs.  - Maintain and update engagement contact list and stakeholder maps.  - Participate in and support planning and logistics for public tabling and events.  - Create visual materials for outreach and communication efforts.  - Assist in drafting engagement strategies and outreach plans.  - Deliverables will vary based on project needs.    SUPERVISION  Direct supervision from a Planner/Project Manager on the team, as well as the Deputy Director and Director of the team. Frequent in-person meetings and trainings will be held with the intern to teach them about HPD, valuable professional skills, and advance their internship work. Our team values growth, mentorship, and open communication, and we all learn from each other.    WORK SCHEDULE:  19 hours per week, spread across 3 or 4 days per week (Mon-Thurs), duration of 6 weeks from July-August 2026.    LOCATION:  In-person: NYC HPD, 100 Gold St, New York, NY 10038    NOTE:  Preferred Skills (not required):   - Interest in urban planning, public engagement, public service, or community development.  - Strong writing and communication skills, with some research experience.  - Familiarity with social media tools and some basic skills in Adobe Creative Suite and Canva.  - Comfort collaborating and working in small teams and independently.  - Ability to take initiative and meet deadlines.

column5: Communications Fellow – FLIP National
column6: WHO WE ARE:  ""FLIP" is an acronym; it stands for First-Generation Low-Income Partnership. Training is provided for all of the things we ask of fellows to do in the fellowship.    WORK SCHEDULE:  Weekly check-in time slots are TBD before the fellowship begins for the summer and is based on the stated availability of fellows selected for the fellowship. Evenings, late nights and weekends are all possibilities for meeting times both for internal mandatory meetings and for meetings with prospective or current chapters. When a fellow is given a task, it is of less concern how much time the fellow takes to complete the task and of more concern that the task actually gets completed.
