Please fill out the application form BEFORE submitting your application on this platform.  - If you are assigned to a team as part of being selected for the fellowship, that does not preclude you from working on projects that fall under the purview of other teams in the fellowship. column5: Community Justice Alternatives: Court Operations Intern - (Midtown Community Justice Center)
column6: The Center for Justice Innovation (formerly the Center for Court Innovation) is a non-profit organization that works with communities and justice systems to advance equity, increase safety, and help individuals and communities thrive. The Center's goal is to identify and resolve as early as possible the challenges that bring people into the criminal and civil legal systems. It does this in a number of ways—by developing and running programs that reduce the need for incarceration and enhance economic opportunity, conducting original research to identify what works, and sharing what we learn from our programming and research with those seeking to transform the justice system around the world.    The Center is an 800-employee, $100 million nonprofit that accomplishes its vision through three pillars of work: creating and scaling operating programs to test new ideas and solve problems, performing original research to determine what works (and what doesn’t), and providing expert assistance and policy guidance to justice reformers around the world.    Operating Programs  The Center’s operating programs, including the award-winning Red Hook Community Justice Center and Midtown Community Justice Center, test new ideas, solve difficult problems, and attempt to achieve systemic change within the justice system. Our projects include community-based violence prevention programs, alternatives to incarceration, reentry initiatives, and court-based initiatives that reduce the use of unnecessary incarceration and promote positive individual and family change. Through this programming, we have produced tangible results like safer streets, reduced incarceration, and improved neighborhood perceptions of justice.    Research  The Center's research teams are staffed with social scientists, data analysts, and lawyers who are academically-trained or have lived experience and who conduct research in the U.S. and globally on diverse criminal-legal system and justice issues. Their work includes evaluating programs and policies; conducting exploratory, community-based studies; and providing research translation and strategic planning for system actors. The Center has published studies on topics including court and jail reform, intimate partner violence, restorative justice, gun violence, reentry, sixth amendment rights, and progressive prosecution. The research teams strive to make their work meaningful and actionable to the communities they work with, policymakers, and practitioners.    Policy & Expert Assistance  The Center provides hands-on, planning and implementation assistance to a wide range of jurisdictions in areas of reform such as problem-solving courts (e.g., community courts, treatment courts, domestic violence courts), tribal justice, reducing incarceration and the use of fines/fees and reducing crime and violence. Our current expert assistance takes many forms, including help with analyzing data, strategic planning and consultation, policy guidance, and hosting site visits to its operating programs in the New York City area.     THE OPPORTUNITY    Launched in 1993, the award-winning Midtown Community Justice Center is one of the country’s first problem-solving courts. Seeking to reduce crime and incarceration and increase public trust in justice, the Midtown Community Justice Center works with neighborhood stakeholders to improve Midtown Manhattan. The court responds creatively to low-level offending, seeking alternatives that are restorative to the community. In keeping with that goal, Midtown also operates upstream programming to divert adults and young people from prosecution.    The Center for Justice Innovation operates Project Reset, New York City's pre-arraignment diversion program, city-wide. Operating in collaboration with the New York Police Department, District Attorney’s Offices, and the Mayor’s Office of Criminal Justice, Project Reset seeks to create a proportionate response to low-level crime by avoiding the use of incarceration and the potential harms associated with the traditional criminal justice process. Traditionally, Project Reset participants complete programming in advance of their court date in lieu of prosecution. Recently, the Midtown Community Justice Center began offering Rapid Reset, which offers the same diversion opportunity to Project Reset-eligible people who show up to court.    The Midtown Community Justice Center is seeking an Intern to join Community Justice Alternatives – a team that provides alternative criminal legal responses to low level crime that centers healing and connections to the community. Interns will have the opportunity to engage in broader criminal justice projects across Midtown Community Justice Center as interested. Midtown Community Justice Center’s portfolio currently includes court-based, community-based, and voluntary programs, which includes an Emerging Adult Court, Misdemeanor Mental Health Court, diversion programming, harm reduction services, and various alternatives to incarceration (ATI) programs that offer pre- and post-plea opportunities.    Reporting to the Court Operations Manager, the Intern will be staffed on the Midtown Community Justice Center’s Community Justice Alternatives team and work closely with its court-based and diversion teams. The Intern may also be called upon to support other programs and initiatives at Midtown Community Justice Center as needed.     Responsibilities include but are not limited to:  • Support community members and participants on-site at Midtown Community Justice Center with the support of Community Justice Alternatives team;  • Assist intakes, screenings, and the scheduling and rescheduling mandated participants;  • Collaborate with a broad range of criminal justice, city government, and community partners;  • Cover the main phone line, including answering all incoming calls, taking messages, and connecting callers to the appropriate staff or other agencies where needed;  • Sit at the front desk as assigned to greet visitors, collect basic information, ensure clients’ needs are addressed in a timely and professional manner, notify appropriate staff of client arrivals and incoming calls, and maintain a professional, warm, and welcoming environment;  • Assist with the distribution of MetroCards and ATI phones to clients and log all necessary information;  • Provide direct services to program participants or voluntary participants, including linkages to partner organizations and providing accommodations on-site, as needed;  • Maintain appropriate participant information in electronic databases and hard files, including intake assessments, screenings, and compliance information;  • Attend trainings supporting criminal justice, social service, and procedural and restorative justice work, as offered by the Center for Justice Innovation and its partners, as appropriate;  • Engage in other tasks to advance the intern’s learning and serving the Midtown community.    Qualifications:  Candidates must be a current undergraduate or graduate student who will receive academic credit for an unpaid internship placement. The ideal candidate will be a bright, energetic self-starter seeking to gain experience in criminal courts, justice reform, and non-profit work. Excellent interpersonal skills required. Candidate must be willing to work with diverse communities in a comfortable and non-judgmental manner. Excellent written and verbal communication and computer skills required.    Position Type:  Part-time student intern; hours flexible based on academic schedule and requirements. Developed in collaboration with the program and student.      Location:  Manhattan, NY, specifically the Midtown Community Justice Center (314 W 54th Street, New York, NY 10019).

column5: Communications Archivist Intern – NYC Employees' Retirement System (NYCERS)
column6: WHO WE ARE:  The New York City Employees’ Retirement System (NYCERS) was founded by the New York State Legislature in 1920 with 13,331 members. Today, NYCERS has grown into the largest municipal public employee retirement system in the United States with more than 430,000 active members and retirees. NYCERS is a defined benefit retirement plan. Defined benefit retirement plans for public sector employees offer benefits which are defined in law. Generally, retirement allowances payable from such plans are based on a member’s years of service, age and compensation base. Other types of benefits such as loans, disability and death benefits are also offered and specified in law. All benefits payable are funded by employee and employer contributions and from earnings on the invested assets of the system.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  NYCERS is seeking a meticulous and talented communications intern to support the goals and work of the Communications Division.     The Communications Division creates and implements NYCERS’ communication strategy and develops creative solutions that proactively engage internal and external clients and stakeholders. The division collaborates with other divisions to prepare and/or update artifacts (brochures, fact sheets, letters, forms and presentations) that NYCERS’ clients (members, retirees, beneficiaries) use to make decisions about their pension accounts. The Communications Division also manages content, graphics, and multimedia on NYCERS’ website and secure self-service portal (NYCERS.org and MyNYCERS.org); and collaborates with internal stakeholders to share information and engage employees through internal channels.  As NYCERS moves away from paper to digital processes, the intern, under direct supervision of a Communications associate, will work to archive NYCERS paper artifacts, including forms, brochures, fact sheets, and other paper documents. As the largest public health nonprofit serving New York City, we improve health outcomes and help communities thrive by providing services directly to vulnerable families, supporting community-based organizations through long-standing public-private partnerships, and bridging the gap between healthcare and community services. column5: (CQI Intern) – (BronxWorks)
column6: WHO WE ARE:    BronxWorks is a $140 million nonprofit human services organization serving over 60,000 individuals and families annually across New York City. For more than 50 years, we have worked to feed, shelter, house, teach, and support our community through a comprehensive portfolio of programs including homelessness prevention, supportive housing, workforce development, early childhood education, and family services. We operate 60+ sites across the Bronx and beyond, delivering integrated services designed to stabilize families, build economic mobility, and strengthen neighborhoods. Our work is grounded in data, equity, compliance, and continuous quality improvement.      DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:    Support the Director of Program Quality & Evaluation and Business Systems Manager in advancing Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) initiatives    -Assist with data cleaning, aggregation, and validation using de-identified or sample datasets  -Develop dashboards and summary reports using program-level or aggregated performance data  -Conduct research on best practices in quality assurance, evaluation, compliance, and data governance  -Help document workflows, SOPs, and CQI processes  -Support internal audit preparation using non-confidential documentation and structured review tools  -Analyze trends in performance metrics to identify operational improvement opportunities  -Assist in preparing materials for leadership presentations and cross-departmental meetings  -Support special projects related to systems improvement, automation, and reporting efficiency    Note: All work involving data will adhere strictly to BronxWorks’ confidentiality, data security, and compliance protocols. The intern will not access or handle protected client-level information unless specifically authorized and trained under agency data protection policies.    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:    -Application of CQI methodology within a large human services organization  -Ethical data handling and nonprofit data governance practices  -Aggregated data analysis and performance reporting  -Dashboard development and data visualization  -Cross-functional collaboration in a regulated environment  -Translating data into actionable, leadership-ready insights  -Professional standards related to confidentiality, HIPAA-informed practices, and client privacy protection    SUPERVISION:    The intern will be jointly supervised by the Director of Program Quality & Evaluation.    Supervision structure includes:    -One-on-one supervision meetings  -Bi-weekly structured project check-ins  -Clear scope of work and defined deliverables  -Ongoing feedback and mentorship  -Orientation to BronxWorks’ confidentiality, compliance, and data security policies prior to beginning project work    If exposure to live systems is required for learning purposes, access will be limited, role-based, and compliant with agency data protection standards. Most analytical work will utilize de-identified, aggregated, or sample datasets.    WORK SCHEDULE:    The internship requires completion of 133 hours between July 13 and August 21.    Proposed schedule:    19 hours per week over 6 weeks  Business hours: Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM  Weekly supervision meeting (day/time confirmed upon selection)  Final schedule established at start to ensure completion of required hours    LOCATION:  Hybrid  60 East Tremont Avenue  Bronx, NY 10453    Intern will work both remotely and on-site at BronxWorks’ central administrative office. On-site presence expected 1–2 days per week, particularly during onboarding and collaborative project meetings.        NOTE: This role is best suited for students with strong technical proficiency (advanced Excel required; familiarity with Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools preferred). Intern must complete agency onboarding, including confidentiality and data security training, prior to accessing systems.  Position focuses on systems-level improvement, aggregated data analysis, and quality infrastructure — not direct client service.  All work will align with BronxWorks’ privacy, compliance, and ethical standards.

column5: Business Development Intern – MacroBreed
column6: WHO WE ARE:  MacroBreed is modernizing seaweed aquaculture by leveraging genomics to increase the production and value of farmed seaweed through selective breeding. The costs of production for seaweed farming are too high to compete with wild harvests and imports. Breeding will enhance the value of kelp, opening new markets and help the industry scale towards a more sustainable and regenerative future. Our initial targets include tripling harvestable biomass, increasing polysaccharide content, and increasing thermal tolerance compared to current commercial practices.    DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:  1. Competitor Landscape  Identify  key competitors in the seaweed breeding, cultivation, and biotech space, including startups, established aquaculture firms, and research institutions. Analyze their product offerings, breeding technologies, geographic focus, partnerships, and positioning. Maintain a living competitor database that can be updated as the industry evolves.  2. Market Sizing & Trends  Research the current and projected size of the global seaweed market across relevant segments (food & beverage, animal feed, bioplastics, pharmaceuticals, biostimulants, etc.). Track emerging trends such as advances in selective breeding, sustainable aquaculture, and demand driven by food security and climate initiatives. Summarize findings in clear reports and presentations for internal stakeholders.  3. Customer Segments  Map out the key customer segments purchasing seaweed genetics, seedstock, or cultivation solutions — including commercial seaweed farmers, food manufacturers, biotech companies, and research organizations. Develop basic customer profiles that capture their needs, pain points, purchasing behavior, and willingness to pay.  4. Regulatory Environment  Survey the regulatory landscape governing seaweed cultivation and breeding across key markets (e.g., US, EU, Southeast Asia). Identify relevant permitting requirements, biosafety regulations, import/export restrictions, and emerging policy developments that could impact the company's operations or expansion plans.    INTERN WILL LEARN/DEVELOP:  *Market Intelligence  *Gain hands-on experience with market sizing methodologies, trend analysis, and competitive benchmarking. These are foundational skills for any business development or strategy career.  *Strategic Thinking  *By connecting competitor behavior, market trends, customer needs, and regulatory constraints into a coherent picture, they'll practice thinking like a strategist. These skills will translate to why it matters for the business.  *Communication & Presentation  *Translating complex research into clear reports, summaries, and presentations will strengthen both their written and visual communication skills.    QUALIFICATIONS:  Completed some of the following: Introduction to Business or Business Foundations, Microeconomics, Business Communications, Introductory Statistics or Data Analysis  Environmental Studies, Marine Science, or Sustainability coursework is a plus    SUPERVISION  CEO Gary Molano will supervise two remote mandatory meetings a week to review weekly goals and to recap weekly achievements. Meetings will occur on Google Meet.  Gary will provide mentorship support on academia - commercialization path, blue biotech, scaling strategies, and genomics    WORK SCHEDULE:  DAYS/TIME:   - Mandatory 1 Hour Meetings Tuesday/Thursday Afternoon TBD  - Other meetings may be scheduled during the week as needed  - 19 hours per week. Work hours are flexible, but would prefer Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday afternoons (1-5pm)    LOCATION:  Virtual
